title.raw: 卷八十九 晉書15: 列傳四 桑維翰 趙瑩 劉昫 馮玉 殷鵬 Volume 89 Book of Later Jin 15: Biographies 4 - Sang Weihan, Zhao Ying, Liu Xu, Feng Yu, Yin Peng

sentences.zh: 桑維翰，字國僑，洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Sang Weihan, styled Guoqiao, was a native of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Weihan, whose style was Guoqiao, came from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 父珙，事河南尹張全義為客將。

translations.literal: His father Gong served Zhang Quanyi, Intendant of Henan, as a client officer.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gong had served as a client officer under Zhang Quanyi, the Intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 維翰身短面廣，殆非常人，既壯，每對鑒自嘆曰：「七尺之身，安如一尺之面！

translations.literal: Weihan was short in stature but broad of face, almost unlike an ordinary man. Once grown, whenever he faced a mirror he would sigh and say: "A body of seven feet—how can it be worthy of a face of one foot!
translations.idiomatic: Weihan was short but had an unusually broad face. After he came of age, he would often sigh before his mirror and say, "A seven-foot body—what good is a one-foot face!

sentences.zh: 」由是慨然有公輔之望。

translations.literal: " From this he came to aspire fervently to high ministerial office.
translations.idiomatic: " From that time he burned with ambition to reach the highest offices of state.

sentences.zh: （《三楚新錄》：馬希範入覲，途經淮上，時桑維翰旅遊楚、泗間，知其來，遽謁之曰：「仆聞楚之為國，挾天子而令諸侯，其勢不可謂卑也；

translations.literal: (The 《New Records of the Three Chu Regions》 says: When Ma Xifan went to court and passed along the Huai, Sang Weihan was then traveling between Chu and Si. Learning of his arrival, he hurried to call on him and said: "I have heard that as a state Chu holds the Son of Heaven and commands the feudal lords—its position cannot be called lowly;
translations.idiomatic: (The 《New Records of the Three Chu Regions》 relates that when Ma Xifan went to court and passed the Huai, Sang Weihan was traveling in the Chu and Si region. Hearing of his approach, he went at once to pay his respects and said, "I understand that Chu holds the emperor hostage and orders the feudal lords about—its standing can hardly be called modest;

sentences.zh: 加以利盡南海，公室大富。

translations.literal: moreover its profits exhaust the Southern Sea and the royal house is greatly enriched.
translations.idiomatic: and with profits drawn from the far south, the royal treasury is flush.

sentences.zh: 足下之來也，非傾府庫之半，則不足以供芻粟之費。

translations.literal: Your coming here will require no less than half the treasury to cover fodder and grain expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Your journey will cost at least half the treasury in fodder and grain alone.

sentences.zh: 今仆貧者，敢以萬金為請，惟足下濟之。

translations.literal: Now I, your humble servant, am poor and venture to request ten thousand in gold—may Your Lordship assist me."
translations.idiomatic: I am a poor man and dare ask ten thousand in gold—please grant it."

sentences.zh: 」希範輕薄公子，睹維翰形短而腰長，語魯而且醜，不覺絕倒而笑。

translations.literal: Xifan was a frivolous young lord. Seeing Weihan's short body and long waist, his speech crude and ugly, he could not help but burst out laughing.
translations.idiomatic: Xifan was a frivolous young noble. Seeing Weihan's short torso and long waist, hearing his rough and homely speech, he doubled over with laughter.

sentences.zh: 既而與數百縑，維翰大怒，拂衣而去。）〉

translations.literal: He then gave him several hundred bolts of silk. Weihan flew into a rage, shook out his robes, and left.)〉
translations.idiomatic: He then gave him a few hundred bolts of silk. Weihan was furious, flung aside his robe, and stalked off.)]

sentences.zh: 性明惠，善詞賦。

translations.literal: By nature he was bright and clever and skilled at rhapsodies and fu.
translations.idiomatic: He was naturally quick-witted and excelled at poetry and fu.

sentences.zh: （《春渚記聞》：桑維翰試進士，有司嫌其姓，黜之。

translations.literal: (The 《Spring Islet Miscellany》 says: When Sang Weihan sat for the jinshi examination, the authorities disliked his surname and failed him.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Spring Islet Miscellany》 records that when Sang Weihan took the jinshi examination, the examiners rejected him because of his surname.

sentences.zh: 或勸勿試，維翰持鐵硯示人曰：「鐵硯穿，乃改業。

translations.literal: Some urged him not to try again. Weihan held up an iron inkstone and showed people, saying: "When this iron inkstone wears through, then I shall change my profession."
translations.idiomatic: Some advised him to give up, but Weihan held up an iron inkstone and declared, "When this inkstone wears through, only then will I change my calling."

sentences.zh: 」著《日出扶桑賦》以見誌。）〉

translations.literal: " He wrote the 《Rhapsody on the Sun Rising over the Fusang》 to express his resolve.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " He composed the 《Rhapsody on the Sun Rising over the Fusang》 to declare his intent.)]

sentences.zh: 唐同光中，登進士第。

translations.literal: In the Tongguang era of Tang he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tang Tongguang reign he finally earned his jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: （《洛陽縉紳舊聞記》：桑魏公父珙為河南府客將，桑魏公將應舉，父乘間告王雲曰：「某男粗有文性，今被同人相率取解，俟王旨。

translations.literal: (The 《Old Tales Heard among the Gentry of Luoyang》 says: Duke Sang of Wei's father Gong was a client officer of the Henan prefecture. When Duke Sang of Wei was about to take the examinations, his father seized an opportunity to tell Wang Yun: "My son has some rough literary talent. He is now being led by his peers to obtain a provincial degree and awaits Your Highness's instruction."
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Old Tales Heard among the Gentry of Luoyang》 says: The future Duke Sang of Wei's father Gong served as a Henan client officer. When the son was to sit for the examinations, the father found a moment to tell Wang Yun, "My boy has a measure of literary promise. His fellows are taking him to qualify for the provincial exam, and we await your word."

sentences.zh: 」齊王曰：「有男應舉，好，可令秀才來。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi said: "Your son is taking the examinations—good. Have the xiucai come."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi said, "A son taking the exams—that is well. Send the young scholar."

sentences.zh: 」桑相之父趨下再拜。

translations.literal: The future Chancellor Sang's father hurried down and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The future chancellor's father hurried forward and bowed deeply twice.

sentences.zh: 既歸，令子侵早投書啟，獻文字數軸。

translations.literal: After returning home he had his son go early to submit letters and present several scrolls of writing.
translations.idiomatic: Back home, he sent his son early with letters and several scrolls of his work.

sentences.zh: 王請見桑秀才，其父教之趨階，王曰：「不可，既應舉便是貢士。

translations.literal: Wang asked to see Scholar Sang. His father taught him to hurry up the steps. Wang said: "That will not do—once one has entered the examinations one is already a presented scholar."
translations.idiomatic: Wang asked to see Scholar Sang. The father urged him up the steps, but Wang said, "No—once he has entered the examinations he is already a presented scholar."

sentences.zh: 」可歸客司。

translations.literal: " He may return to the guest office."
translations.idiomatic: " He may go back to the guest office."

sentences.zh: 」謂魏公父曰：「他道路不同，莫管他。

translations.literal: He said to Duke Sang of Wei's father: "His path is different—do not trouble him."
translations.idiomatic: He told the father, "Their paths differ—leave him be."

sentences.zh: 」終以客禮見。

translations.literal: In the end he received him with guest ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he received him with the courtesy due a guest.

sentences.zh: 王一見奇之，禮遇頗厚。

translations.literal: At first sight Wang found him remarkable and treated him with considerable favor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang took to him at once and treated him with marked generosity.

sentences.zh: 是年王力言於當時儒臣，且推薦之，由是擢上第。）〉

translations.literal: That year Wang spoke forcefully to the Confucian officials of the day and also recommended him, and thereby he was placed in the top rank.)〉
translations.idiomatic: That year Wang pressed his case among the leading scholars and recommended him, and so he won first place.)]

sentences.zh: 高祖領河陽，辟為掌書記，歷數鎮皆從，及建義太原，首預其謀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu held command of Heyang, he recruited him as chief secretary; through several postings he followed him, and when the righteous enterprise was raised at Taiyuan he was among the first to share in its planning.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Gaozu held Heyang, he took Weihan on as chief secretary. Weihan followed him through successive commands, and when the uprising began at Taiyuan he was among the first to help plan it.

sentences.zh: 復遣為書求援於契丹，果應之。

translations.literal: He again sent him with letters to seek aid from the Khitan, and they indeed responded.
translations.idiomatic: He again sent him with letters to seek Khitan aid, and the Khitan answered the call.

sentences.zh: 俄以趙德鈞發使聘契丹，高祖懼其改謀，命維翰詣幕帳，述其始終利害之義，其約乃定。

translations.literal: Soon Zhao Dejun dispatched envoys to court the Khitan. Gaozu feared they would alter their plans and ordered Weihan to go to the Khitan camp and explain the advantages and disadvantages from beginning to end, and the agreement was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhao Dejun sent envoys to woo the Khitan. Gaozu feared a change of heart and sent Weihan to the Khitan camp to lay out the whole case for and against; only then was the pact secured.

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：趙德鈞以金帛賂契丹主，云：「若立己為帝，請即以見兵南平洛陽，與契丹為兄弟之國，仍許石氏常鎮河東。

translations.literal: (The 《Comprehensive Mirror》 says: Zhao Dejun bribed the Khitan ruler with gold and silk, saying: "If you establish me as emperor, I beg to lead my present forces south to pacify Luoyang, make a brother-state with the Khitan, and still allow the Shi clan to hold Hedong in perpetuity."
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Comprehensive Mirror》 relates that Zhao Dejun bribed the Khitan emperor with gold and silk, saying, "If you make me emperor, I will lead my present forces south to take Luoyang, establish a brotherhood with the Khitan, and let the Shi family keep Hedong forever."

sentences.zh: 」契丹主自以深入敵境，晉安未下，德鈞兵尚強，範延光在其東，又恐山北諸州邀其歸路，欲許德鈞之請。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler himself felt he had penetrated deep into enemy territory; Jin'an was not yet taken, Dejun's forces were still strong, Fan Yanguang lay to his east, and he also feared that the prefectures north of the mountains would cut off his line of retreat—he wished to grant Dejun's request.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler felt he had marched deep into enemy country. Jin'an still held out, Dejun's army remained strong, Fan Yanguang blocked the east, and he feared the northern prefectures might cut his retreat—he was inclined to accept Dejun's offer.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之大懼，亟使維翰見契丹主，說之曰：「大國舉義兵以救孤危，一戰而唐兵瓦解，退守一柵，食盡力窮。

translations.literal: The emperor, hearing this, was greatly afraid and urgently sent Weihan to see the Khitan ruler. He argued: "Your great state raised righteous troops to rescue one in peril. In a single battle Tang forces disintegrated and retreated to hold one palisade; their food is exhausted and their strength spent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was terrified and sent Weihan at once to the Khitan camp. Weihan pleaded, "Your great state raised righteous arms to save us in our extremity. One battle shattered the Tang army; they cling to a single stockade, out of food and spent of strength."

sentences.zh: 趙北平父子不忠不信，畏大國之強，且素蓄異志，按兵觀變，非以死徇國之人，何足可畏，而信其誕妄之辭，貪毫末之利，棄垂成之功乎！

translations.literal: The father and son of Beiping Zhao are disloyal and untrustworthy. They fear your great state's might and have long harbored other designs, holding their troops back to watch how events turn—they are not men who would die for the state. Why should they be feared? Why believe their extravagant falsehoods, covet a trifling gain, and abandon a victory all but won!
translations.idiomatic: The Beiping Zhao and his son are faithless. They fear your power, have long nursed other ambitions, and hold their army idle to watch the turn of events—they are not men who would die for their country. Why fear them? Why credit their wild promises, grasp at a pittance, and throw away a victory within reach!

sentences.zh: 且使晉得天下，將竭中國之財以奉大國，豈此小利之比乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, if Jin gains the realm, it will exhaust the wealth of China to serve your great state—how can that be compared with this petty profit!
translations.idiomatic: And if Jin wins the empire, it will pour out the wealth of China to serve your great state—how does that compare with this petty bribe!

sentences.zh: 」契丹主曰：「爾見捕鼠者乎？

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler said: "Have you seen one who catches rats?"
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler said, "Have you ever seen a rat-catcher?"

sentences.zh: 不備之，猶或嚙傷其手，況大敵乎！

translations.literal: Even without taking precautions, the rat may still bite and wound his hand—how much more so a great foe!
translations.idiomatic: Even unguarded, the rat may still bite his hand—how much more a formidable enemy!

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「今大國已扼其喉，安能嚙人乎！

translations.literal: He replied: "Now your great state has seized them by the throat—how can they bite anyone!"
translations.idiomatic: Weihan answered, "Your great state already has them by the throat—how can they bite anyone now!"

sentences.zh: 」契丹主曰：「吾非有渝前約也，但兵家權謀，不得不爾。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler said: "I am not violating our earlier pact, but in military affairs stratagem compels one to act thus."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler said, "I am not breaking our pact, but military necessity leaves me no choice."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「皇帝以信義救人之急，四海之人俱屬耳目，奈何二三其命，使大義不終，臣竊為皇帝不取也。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your Majesty came in good faith to rescue one in distress. All under heaven are watching—how can you change your word twice over and leave the great cause unfinished? Your servant ventures to think this unworthy of Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Weihan answered, "Your Majesty came in good faith to save us in our need. The whole world is watching—how can you shift your word and leave the great undertaking unfinished? I venture to say this does not become Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」跪於帳前，自旦之暮，涕泣爭之。

translations.literal: He knelt before the tent from dawn till dusk, weeping and disputing the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He knelt before the tent from dawn to dusk, weeping and arguing without cease.

sentences.zh: 契丹乃從之，指帳前石謂德鈞使者曰：「我已許石郎，此石爛，可改矣。」）〉

translations.literal: The Khitan then yielded. Pointing to a stone before the tent he told Dejun's envoy: "I have already promised Lord Shi; when this stone rots, the promise may be changed.")〉
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan relented. Pointing to a stone before the tent he told Dejun's envoy, "I have promised Lord Shi; when this stone crumbles, the promise may change.")]

sentences.zh: 及高祖建號，制授翰林學士、禮部侍郎，知樞密院事。

translations.literal: When Gaozu established his reign title, by imperial order he was appointed Hanlin academician and Vice Minister of Rites, with charge of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu founded his dynasty, he was appointed Hanlin academician and Vice Minister of Rites and put in charge of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋改中書侍郎、平章事、集賢殿大學士，充樞密院使。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Councillor, and Grand Academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies, and made Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Councillor, and Grand Academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies, and confirmed as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 高祖幸夷門，範延光據鄴叛，張從賓復自河、洛舉兵向闕，人心恟恟。

translations.literal: When Gaozu visited Yimen, Fan Yanguang seized Ye and rebelled, and Zhang Congbin again raised troops from the Yellow River and Luoyang regions toward the capital; popular sentiment was in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu went to Yimen, Fan Yanguang rebelled from Ye and Zhang Congbin again marched from the He and Luo region toward the capital; the realm was in uproar.

sentences.zh: 時有人候於維翰者，維翰從容談論，怡怡如也，時皆服其度量。

translations.literal: At the time some came to wait on Weihan. He discussed matters at ease, cheerful and composed, and all then admired his breadth of spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Visitors came to wait on Weihan, but he conversed calmly and cheerfully, and all admired his composure.

sentences.zh: 及楊光遠平鄴，朝廷慮兵驕難制，維翰請速散其眾，尋移光遠鎮洛陽。

translations.literal: When Yang Guangyuan pacified Ye, the court feared that troops grown arrogant would be hard to control. Weihan asked that they be quickly dispersed, and soon Guangyuan was transferred to garrison Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Guangyuan took Ye, the court feared arrogant troops would prove hard to control. Weihan urged their swift dispersal, and Guangyuan was soon transferred to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 光遠由是怏怏，上疏論維翰去公徇私，除改不當，復營邸肆於兩都之下，與民爭利。

translations.literal: Guangyuan was thereby discontented and submitted a memorial accusing Weihan of abandoning the public good for private ends, of improper appointments and dismissals, and of again operating inns and shops under the two capitals to compete with the people for profit.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan was resentful and memorialized that Weihan had put private interest above the public good, made improper appointments, and again ran inns and shops in both capitals to compete with the people for profit.

sentences.zh: 高祖方姑息外將，事不獲已，因授維翰檢校司空、兼侍中，出為相州節度使，時天福四年七月也。

translations.literal: Gaozu was then indulging frontier generals and could not do otherwise; he therefore appointed Weihan Acting Minister of Works with concurrent appointment as Palace Attendant and sent him out as military governor of Xiangzhou—it was the seventh month of the Tianfu fourth year.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was then placating frontier commanders and had no choice; he made Weihan Acting Minister of Works and Palace Attendant and sent him out as governor of Xiangzhou in the seventh month of Tianfu 4.

sentences.zh: 先是，相州管內所獲盜賊，皆籍沒其財產，雲是河朔舊例。

translations.literal: Previously, within the Xiangzhou circuit all captured bandits had their property registered and confiscated, it being said that this was an old custom of the Hebei-Shandong region.
translations.idiomatic: Previously in Xiangzhou all captured thieves had their property confiscated, on the grounds that this was an old Hebei custom.

sentences.zh: 及維翰作鎮，以律無明文，具事以奏之。

translations.literal: When Weihan took command of the circuit, because the statutes had no explicit provision on the matter, he reported the full facts in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When Weihan took the post, finding no explicit statute for the practice, he reported the matter in full to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「桑維翰佐命功全，臨戎寄重，舉一方之往事，合四海之通規，況賊盜之徒，律令具載。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Sang Weihan's merit in assisting the founding is complete, and his trust on the frontier is weighty. He has raised a past practice of one region to accord with the universal rule of the four seas. Moreover, for bandits and robbers the statutes and ordinances are fully set forth."
translations.idiomatic: An edict read, "Sang Weihan's founding merit is complete and his frontier trust weighty. He has brought a local custom into line with empire-wide law. Bandits and robbers are already fully covered by statute."

sentences.zh: 比為撫萬姓而安萬國，豈忍罪一夫而破一家。

translations.literal: We seek to comfort the myriad people and secure the myriad states—how can we bear to punish one man and ruin one household?
translations.idiomatic: We mean to comfort the people and secure the realm—how can we punish one man and destroy a whole household?

sentences.zh: 聞將相之善言，成國家之美事，既資王道，實契人心。

translations.literal: Hearing the good counsel of generals and ministers, we accomplish a fine deed for the state, supporting the royal way and truly meeting the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing wise counsel from our ministers, we accomplish a worthy deed for the state, uphold the royal way, and win the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 今後凡有賊人準格律定罪，不得沒納家資，天下諸州皆準此處分。

translations.literal: Henceforth all thieves shall be sentenced according to statute and regulation, and household property may not be confiscated. All prefectures under heaven shall follow this ruling.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth all thieves shall be sentenced under statute and household property shall not be seized. Every prefecture in the realm shall follow this rule.

sentences.zh: 」自是劫盜之家，皆免籍沒，維翰之力也。

translations.literal: From this time households of robbers were all spared confiscation—this was Weihan's doing.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the families of robbers were spared confiscation—thanks to Weihan.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，移鎮兗州。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to govern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was transferred to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時吐渾都督白承福為契丹所迫，舉眾內附，高祖方通好於契丹，拒而不納。

translations.literal: At that time the Tujue commander Bai Chengfu, pressed by the Khitan, led his people in submission to the interior. Gaozu was then on friendly terms with the Khitan and refused to accept them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Tujue commander Bai Chengfu, harried by the Khitan, led his people to submit to the Jin court. Gaozu was courting the Khitan and refused to accept them.

sentences.zh: 鎮州節度使安重榮患契丹之強，欲謀攻襲，戎師往返路出於真定者，皆潛害之，密與吐渾相結，至是遂納焉，而致於朝。

translations.literal: An Chongrong, military governor of Zhenzhou, resented Khitan strength and wished to plan an attack. Troops coming and going along routes that passed through Zhending he secretly harmed, and he had secretly allied with the Tujue; at this time he therefore accepted them and presented them at court.
translations.idiomatic: An Chongrong, governor of Zhenzhou, resented Khitan power and plotted attack. He secretly harmed troops passing through Zhending and had secretly allied with the Tujue; now he accepted them and sent them to court.

sentences.zh: 既而安重榮抗表請討契丹，且言吐渾之請。

translations.literal: Soon afterward An Chongrong submitted a defiant memorial requesting a campaign against the Khitan and also spoke of the Tujue petition.
translations.idiomatic: Soon An Chongrong submitted a defiant memorial asking to attack the Khitan and citing the Tujue submission.

sentences.zh: 是時安重榮握強兵，據重鎮，恃其驍勇，有飛揚跋扈之志。

translations.literal: At this time An Chongrong held strong troops and occupied a key post, relying on his fierce valor and harboring ambitions to rise arrogantly above others.
translations.idiomatic: An Chongrong then held a strong army and a key post, trusted in his fighting prowess, and nursed overweening ambitions.

sentences.zh: 晉祖覽表，猶豫未決。

translations.literal: The Jin founder read the memorial and hesitated, unable to decide.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin founder read the memorial and hesitated.

sentences.zh: 維翰知重榮已畜奸謀，且懼朝廷違其意，乃密上疏曰：

translations.literal: Weihan knew that Chongrong had already nurtured treacherous designs and also feared the court might go against his wishes; he therefore submitted a secret memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Weihan knew Chongrong already harbored treasonous designs and feared the court might yield to him; he submitted a secret memorial:

sentences.zh: 竊以防未萌之禍亂，立不拔之基扃，上系聖謀，動符天意，非臣淺陋，所可窺圖。

translations.literal: I venture to think that guarding against calamity before it sprouts and establishing a foundation that cannot be uprooted depend on the sage's stratagems and accord with Heaven's intent—matters your servant's shallowness cannot presume to discern.
translations.idiomatic: To guard against disaster before it arises and lay an unshakable foundation rests on your sacred counsel and Heaven's will—matters far beyond my poor understanding.

sentences.zh: 然臣逢世休明，致位通顯，無功報國，省己愧心，其或事系安危，理關家國，茍或緘默，實負君親，是以區區之心，不能自己。

translations.literal: Yet your servant has met an age of glorious peace and reached eminent rank without merit to repay the state. Reflecting on myself I feel shame. If affairs touch security and peril and principle concerns state and family, to keep silent would truly fail sovereign and parent. Therefore this humble heart cannot restrain itself.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I have reached high office in a glorious age without merit to repay the state, and I am ashamed. When affairs touch the realm's safety, silence would betray sovereign and father. I cannot hold my peace.

sentences.zh: 近者，相次得進奏院狀報：吐渾首領白承福已下舉眾內附，鎮州節度使安重榮上表請討契丹。

translations.literal: Recently I have received in succession reports from the Memorial Submission Office: the Tujue leader Bai Chengfu and his followers have led their people in submission, and An Chongrong, military governor of Zhenzhou, has submitted a memorial requesting a campaign against the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I have received successive reports from the Memorial Office: the Tujue leader Bai Chengfu has led his people to submit, and An Chongrong of Zhenzhou has memorialized for a campaign against the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 臣方遙隔朝闕，未測端倪。

translations.literal: Your servant is far from the court and cannot yet discern how matters stand.
translations.idiomatic: I am far from court and cannot yet see how matters stand.

sentences.zh: 竊思陛下頃在並、汾，初罹屯難，師少糧匱，援絕計窮，勢若綴旒，困同懸磬。

translations.literal: I reflect that Your Majesty was lately at Bing and Fen, first encountering hardship in a beleaguered situation: few troops, scarce grain, aid cut off and plans exhausted, your position like a pendant thread, your distress like a hanging chime.
translations.idiomatic: I recall that Your Majesty was lately at Bing and Fen, first beset by hardship: few troops, scarce grain, no allies and no options, your throne hanging by a thread, your plight desperate.

sentences.zh: 契丹控弦玉塞，躍馬龍城，直度陰山，徑絕大漠，萬里赴難，一戰夷兇，救陛下累卵之危，成陛下覆盂之業。

translations.literal: The Khitan strung bows at the Jade Barrier, spurred horses at Dragon City, crossed straight over the Yin Mountains and cut directly across the great desert, coming ten thousand li to aid in distress. In one battle they destroyed the foe, rescued Your Majesty from danger piled like eggs, and accomplished Your Majesty's enterprise secure as an inverted bowl.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan strung their bows at the frontier, spurred their horses from Dragon City, crossed the Yin Mountains and the great desert, marched ten thousand li to your aid, and in one battle destroyed the enemy—saving you from peril piled like eggs and securing your throne as firm as an overturned bowl.

sentences.zh: 皇朝受命，於此六年，彼此通歡，亭障無事。

translations.literal: The dynasty has received the Mandate for six years now; the two sides have exchanged goodwill and the border posts have been untroubled.
translations.idiomatic: Six years have passed since the dynasty received the Mandate; we have exchanged goodwill with them and the frontier has been quiet.

sentences.zh: 雖卑辭降節，屈萬乘之尊，而庇國息民，實數萬之利。

translations.literal: Although humble words and lowered ceremony have bent the dignity of the Son of Heaven, in sheltering the state and giving the people rest the benefit is truly in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Though humble words and lowered ceremony have bent imperial dignity, sheltering the state and giving the people peace has brought benefit beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 今者，安重榮表契丹之罪，方恃勇以請行；

translations.literal: Now An Chongrong has memorialized the Khitan's crimes and is relying on his courage to request action;
translations.idiomatic: Now An Chongrong has listed Khitan crimes and, trusting in his courage, asks to march;

sentences.zh: 白承福畏契丹之強，將假手以報怨。

translations.literal: Bai Chengfu fears Khitan strength and wishes to borrow another's hand to settle a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Chengfu fears Khitan power and would use another's hand to settle his grudge.

sentences.zh: 恐非遠慮，有惑聖聰。

translations.literal: I fear this is not far-sighted counsel and may confuse Your Majesty's judgment.
translations.idiomatic: I fear this is not far-sighted and may mislead Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 方今契丹未可與爭者，有其七焉：契丹數年來最強盛，侵伐鄰國，吞滅諸蕃，救援河東，功成師克。

translations.literal: At present there are seven reasons why the Khitan cannot be contested: for several years the Khitan have been at their strongest, invading neighboring states, swallowing the various frontier peoples, rescuing Hedong, achieving their task and their army victorious.
translations.idiomatic: At present there are seven reasons the Khitan cannot be fought: for years they have been at their peak, raiding neighbors, absorbing frontier peoples, rescuing Hedong, and winning every campaign.

sentences.zh: 山後之名藩大郡，盡入封疆；

translations.literal: The famous prefectures and great commanderies beyond the mountains have all entered their borders;
translations.idiomatic: The famous prefectures beyond the mountains have all fallen to them;

sentences.zh: 中華之精甲利兵，悉歸廬帳。

translations.literal: the finest armor and keenest weapons of China have all gone to their tents.
translations.idiomatic: and China's finest armor and weapons have passed to their camps.

sentences.zh: 即今土地廣而人民眾，戎器備而戰馬多。

translations.literal: At present their lands are broad and their people numerous, their weapons ready and their war-horses many.
translations.idiomatic: Today their lands are vast, their people numerous, their arms ready, and their horses plentiful.

sentences.zh: 此未可與爭者一也。

translations.literal: This is the first reason they cannot be contested.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first reason they cannot be fought.

sentences.zh: 契丹自告捷之後，鋒銳氣雄；

translations.literal: Since reporting victory the Khitan blades are sharp and their spirit bold;
translations.idiomatic: Since their victories the Khitan are sharp and bold;

sentences.zh: 南軍因敗衄已來，心沮膽怯。

translations.literal: the southern armies, since their defeats, have hearts discouraged and courage timid.
translations.idiomatic: while our southern armies, since their defeats, are discouraged and timid.

sentences.zh: 況秋夏雖稔，而帑廩無餘；

translations.literal: Moreover, though autumn and summer have brought harvests, the treasuries have no surplus;
translations.idiomatic: Though the harvests have been fair, the treasuries are empty;

sentences.zh: 黎庶雖安，而貧弊益甚；

translations.literal: though the common people are at peace, poverty and distress grow worse;
translations.idiomatic: though the people are at peace, poverty grows worse;

sentences.zh: 戈甲雖備，而鍛礪未精；

translations.literal: though arms and armor are on hand, forging and sharpening are not yet perfected;
translations.idiomatic: though arms are stocked, they are not well forged;

sentences.zh: 士馬雖多，而訓練未至。

translations.literal: though troops and horses are many, training has not yet reached its goal.
translations.idiomatic: and though troops and horses are plentiful, they are not well trained.

sentences.zh: 此未可與爭者二也。

translations.literal: This is the second reason they cannot be contested.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second reason they cannot be fought.

sentences.zh: 契丹與國家，恩義非輕，信誓甚篤，雖多求取，未至侵淩，豈可先發釁端，自為戎首。

translations.literal: Between the Khitan and the state, favor and obligation are not light, and sworn faith is very firm. Though they have made many demands, they have not yet reached the point of invasion and oppression. How can we first raise the banner of strife and make ourselves leader of the war?
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan and our state share deep obligations and firm oaths. Though they have demanded much, they have not yet invaded us. How can we strike first and make ourselves the aggressor?

sentences.zh: 縱使因茲大克，則後患仍存；

translations.literal: Even if through this we achieved a great victory, later troubles would still remain;
translations.idiomatic: Even if we won a great victory, later troubles would remain;

sentences.zh: 其或偶失沈機，則追悔何及。

translations.literal: and if by chance we missed a deep opportunity, what regret could make up for it?
translations.idiomatic: and if we missed our chance, regret would come too late.

sentences.zh: 兵者兇器也，戰者危事也，茍議輕舉，安得萬全。

translations.literal: Arms are an inauspicious instrument and battle a perilous affair. If we rashly discuss and act lightly, how can we be wholly secure?
translations.idiomatic: Arms are ill omens and war a perilous business. Rash counsel cannot promise safety.

sentences.zh: 此未可與爭者三也。

translations.literal: This is the third reason they cannot be contested.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third reason they cannot be fought.

sentences.zh: 王者用兵，觀釁而動。

translations.literal: When a true king employs arms, he watches for a breach and then moves.
translations.idiomatic: A true king uses arms only when he sees an opening.

sentences.zh: 是以漢宣帝得志於匈奴，因單于之爭立；

translations.literal: Thus Emperor Xuan of Han achieved his aim against the Xiongnu because of contention over who would be chanyu;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan of Han prevailed over the Xiongnu because the chanyu succession was disputed;

sentences.zh: 唐太宗立功於突厥，由頡利之不道。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong of Tang won merit against the Turks because Jieli's conduct was unrighteous.
translations.idiomatic: and Emperor Taizong of Tang defeated the Turks because Jieli was unjust.

sentences.zh: 方今契丹主抱雄武之量，有戰伐之機，部族輯睦，蕃國畏伏，土地無災，孳畜繁庶，蕃漢雜用，國無釁隙。

translations.literal: At present the Khitan ruler embraces a heroic and martial capacity and possesses the opportunity for campaigning. His tribes are harmonious, the frontier states fear and submit, the land is free of calamity, livestock are plentiful, Khitan and Chinese are used together, and the state has no breach through which to strike.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Khitan ruler is bold and martial, his tribes united, the frontier peoples submissive, the land free of disaster, livestock plentiful, Khitan and Chinese serving together, and the state without weakness.

sentences.zh: 此未可與爭者四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth reason they cannot be contested.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth reason they cannot be fought.

sentences.zh: 引弓之民，遷徙鳥舉，行逐水草，軍無饋運，居無竈幕，住無營柵，便苦澀，任勞役，不畏風雷，不顧饑渴，皆華人之所不能。

translations.literal: The bow-drawing peoples move like birds in migration, traveling after grass and water. Their armies need no supply transport; they dwell without stoves or tents, halt without camps or palisades. They are accustomed to bitterness, accept hard labor, do not fear wind and thunder, and do not heed hunger and thirst—all things Chinese cannot do.
translations.idiomatic: The bowmen move like migrating birds, following grass and water. Their armies need no supply trains; they live without stoves or tents, camp without walls. They endure hardship, accept toil, fear neither storm nor hunger—things Chinese cannot match.

sentences.zh: 此未可與爭者五也。

translations.literal: This is the fifth reason they cannot be contested.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth reason they cannot be fought.

sentences.zh: 契丹皆騎士，利在坦途；

translations.literal: The Khitan are all horsemen and profit on level ground;
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan are horsemen who thrive on open ground;

sentences.zh: 中國用徒兵，喜於隘險。

translations.literal: China employs foot soldiers and favors narrow defiles.
translations.idiomatic: China relies on infantry and favors narrow terrain.

sentences.zh: 趙魏之北，燕薊之南，千里之間，地平如砥，步騎之便，較然可知。

translations.literal: North of Zhao and Wei, south of Yan and Ji, for a thousand li the land is level as a whetstone—the relative advantage of infantry and cavalry can clearly be compared.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhao and Wei north to Yan and Ji south, a thousand li of land lies flat as a whetstone—the advantage of horse over foot is obvious.

sentences.zh: 國家若與契丹相持，則必屯兵邊上。

translations.literal: If the state contends with the Khitan, it must mass troops on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: If we fight the Khitan, we must mass troops on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 少則懼強敵之眾，固須堅壁以自全；

translations.literal: If few, we fear the enemy's numbers and must hold fast behind walls to preserve ourselves;
translations.idiomatic: With too few, we fear their numbers and must hold behind walls;

sentences.zh: 多則患飛免之勞，必須逐寇而速返。

translations.literal: if many, we suffer the toil of chasing fleeting prey and must pursue raiders and return swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: with too many, we exhaust ourselves chasing raiders who flee and must return at once.

sentences.zh: 我歸而彼至，我出而彼回，則禁衛之驍雄，疲於奔命，鎮、定之封境，略無遺民。

translations.literal: We return and they arrive; we go out and they withdraw—then the elite of the palace guard wear themselves out in desperate marches, and within the borders of Zhen and Ding scarcely a subject remains.
translations.idiomatic: We withdraw and they come; we march out and they withdraw—the palace guard exhaust themselves in endless marches, and Zhen and Ding are left nearly depopulated.

sentences.zh: 此未可與爭者六也。

translations.literal: This is the sixth reason they cannot be contested.
translations.idiomatic: This is the sixth reason they cannot be fought.

sentences.zh: 議者以陛下於契丹有所供億，謂之耗蠹；

translations.literal: Critics say Your Majesty's gifts to the Khitan are a drain and waste;
translations.idiomatic: Critics call Your Majesty's gifts to the Khitan a drain on the treasury;

sentences.zh: 有所卑遜，謂之屈辱。

translations.literal: and your humble deference they call humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: and your deference they call humiliation.

sentences.zh: 微臣所見，則曰不然。

translations.literal: Your humble servant's view is that this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: I say they are mistaken.

sentences.zh: 且以漢祖英雄，猶輸貨於冒頓；

translations.literal: Moreover, the heroic Founder of Han still sent goods to Modu;
translations.idiomatic: Even the heroic Founder of Han sent tribute to Modu;

sentences.zh: 神堯武略，尚稱臣於可汗。

translations.literal: and Divine Valor with martial strategy still styled himself subject to the qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: and Emperor Taizu still styled himself subject to the qaghan.

sentences.zh: 此謂達於權變，善於屈伸，所損者微，所利者大。

translations.literal: This is called mastering expedient change and skill in bending and stretching—what is lost is slight, what is gained is great.
translations.idiomatic: This is mastery of expedient policy—small loss for great gain.

sentences.zh: 必若因茲交構，遂成釁隙，自此則歲歲征發，日日轉輸，困天下之生靈，空國家之府藏，此為耗蠹，不亦甚乎！

translations.literal: If through this we provoke conflict and create a breach, from then on there will be campaigns year after year and transport day after day, distressing all living beings under heaven and emptying the state's treasuries—is this not a far greater drain and waste!
translations.idiomatic: If we provoke war and open a breach, year after year we will levy troops and day after day haul supplies, grinding down the people and emptying the treasury—is that not the greater waste!

sentences.zh: 兵戈既起，將帥擅權，武吏武臣，過求姑息，邊藩遠郡，得以驕矜，外剛內柔，上陵下替，此為屈辱，又非多乎！

translations.literal: Once arms are raised, generals usurp authority, military officers and martial ministers demand excessive indulgence, frontier prefectures and distant commanderies grow arrogant, outwardly hard but inwardly soft, superiors overborne and subordinates displaced—this is humiliation, and is it not far greater!
translations.idiomatic: Once war begins, generals seize power, military men demand indulgence, frontier governors grow arrogant, the strong bully the weak—this is the real humiliation, and is it not far worse!

sentences.zh: 此未可與爭者七也。

translations.literal: This is the seventh reason they cannot be contested.
translations.idiomatic: This is the seventh reason they cannot be fought.

sentences.zh: 願陛下思社稷之大計，采將相之善謀，勿聽樊噲之空言，宜納婁敬之逆耳。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to consider the great plan for altars of soil and grain, adopt the good counsel of generals and ministers, not heed Fan Kuai's empty words, and accept Lou Jing's unwelcome advice.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to weigh the fate of the realm, heed wise counsel, reject Fan Kuai's bluster, and accept Lou Jing's unwelcome truth.

sentences.zh: 然後訓撫士卒，養育黔黎，積穀聚人，勸農習戰，以俟國有九年之積，兵有十倍之強，主無內憂，民有餘力，便可以觀彼之變，待彼之衰，用己之長，攻彼之短，舉無不克，動必成功。

translations.literal: Then train and comfort the troops, nurture the black-haired people, store grain and gather men, encourage farming and drill for battle, until the state has nine years' stores, the army tenfold strength, the ruler no inner worries, and the people surplus strength—then we may watch their changes, await their decline, use our strengths against their weaknesses, and in every undertaking succeed without fail.
translations.idiomatic: Then train the troops, nurture the people, store grain, encourage farming and drill for war, until the state has nine years' reserves and the army tenfold strength, the throne secure and the people at ease—then watch for their changes, await their decline, strike with our strengths at their weaknesses, and succeed in every move.

sentences.zh: 此計之上者也，惟陛下熟思之。

translations.literal: This is the highest plan—may Your Majesty ponder it deeply.
translations.idiomatic: This is the best course—may Your Majesty consider it carefully.

sentences.zh: 臣又以鄴都襟帶山河，表裏形勢，原田沃衍，戶賦殷繁，乃河朔之名藩，實國家之巨屏。

translations.literal: Your servant further notes that the Ye capital girds mountains and rivers with inner and outer strategic strength, its fields fertile and broad, its households and taxes abundant—it is a famous bulwark of Hebei-Shandong and truly a great screen for the state.
translations.idiomatic: I further note that Ye girds mountains and rivers, its fields fertile and its taxes heavy—it is the great bulwark of Hebei and the realm's chief shield.

sentences.zh: 即今主帥赴闕，軍府無人，臣竊思慢藏誨盜之言，恐非勇夫重閉之意，願回深慮，免起奸謀。

translations.literal: At present the commander has gone to court and the military headquarters is unmanned. I reflect on the saying that careless storage teaches theft and fear this is not the intent of a brave man who double-bars his doors. I beg you to reconsider deeply and forestall treacherous designs.
translations.idiomatic: Now the commander has gone to court and the headquarters is empty. I recall that careless storage invites theft—this is no time to leave the gates unbarred. I beg deep reconsideration lest treason arise.

sentences.zh: 欲希陛下暫整和鑾，略謀巡幸。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will for a time put the imperial carriage in order and plan a brief tour.
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will prepare the imperial carriage and plan a brief tour.

sentences.zh: 雖櫛風沐雨，上勞於聖躬；

translations.literal: Though combing wind and bathing in rain may weary Your sacred person,
translations.idiomatic: Though wind and rain may weary Your Majesty,

sentences.zh: 而杜漸防微，實資於睿略。

translations.literal: yet checking what is nascent and guarding against what is slight truly depends on sagacious strategy.
translations.idiomatic: checking trouble at its root truly depends on sagacious foresight.

sentences.zh: 省方展義，今也其時。

translations.literal: To tour the regions and display righteousness—now is the time.
translations.idiomatic: To tour the realm and display imperial virtue—now is the time.

sentences.zh: 臣受主恩深，憂國情切，智小謀大，理淺詞繁，俯伏惟懼於僭逾，裨補或希於萬一，謹冒死以聞。

translations.literal: Your servant has received deep grace from his lord and is keen in concern for the state. My wisdom is small yet my plans are large, my reasoning shallow yet my words many. Prostrate, I fear overstepping, yet hope in one case in ten thousand to be of help. I venture to report at the risk of death.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply favored and keenly concerned for the state, I offer small wisdom for great matters, shallow reasoning in many words. I fear overstepping yet hope to help in the smallest measure, and report at the risk of my life.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，留中不出。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and kept within, not released.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and kept within the palace.

sentences.zh: 高祖召使人於內寢，傳密旨於維翰曰：「朕比以北面事之，煩懣不快，今省所奏，釋然如醒。

translations.literal: Gaozu summoned an envoy to the inner sleeping chamber and conveyed a secret order to Weihan, saying: "Lately, in serving them as the northern vassal, I have been vexed and displeased; now, having examined your memorial, I feel relieved as though awakened from sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu summoned an envoy to his private chamber and sent Weihan a secret message: "Serving the Khitan as their northern vassal has left me weary and unhappy. Reading your memorial, I feel as though I have woken from a long sleep.

sentences.zh: 朕計已決，卿可無憂。」

translations.literal: My plan is already decided; you need not worry."
translations.idiomatic: My mind is made up. You need not worry."

sentences.zh: 七年夏，高祖駕在鄴都，維翰自鎮來朝，改授晉昌軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the summer of the seventh year, Gaozu's carriage was at Ye; Weihan came from his command to court and was reassigned as military governor of the Jinchang army.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the seventh year, while Gaozu was at Ye, Weihan came in from his post to pay court and was reassigned military governor of Jinchang.

sentences.zh: 少帝嗣位，征拜侍中，監修國史。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded to the throne, he was summoned and appointed Palace Attendant and charged with compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor took the throne, Weihan was summoned as Palace Attendant and put in charge of compiling the dynastic history.

sentences.zh: 頻上言請與契丹和，為上將景延廣所否。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials asking to make peace with the Khitan, but was rejected by the commander-in-chief Jing Yanguang.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized the throne urging peace with the Khitan, only to be overruled by the supreme commander Jing Yanguang.

sentences.zh: 明年，楊光遠構契丹，有澶淵之役，凡制敵下令，皆出於延廣，維翰與諸相無所與之。

translations.literal: The next year Yang Guangyuan colluded with the Khitan, and there was the campaign at Chanyuan; all orders for controlling the enemy came from Yanguang, and Weihan and the other chancellors had no part in them.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Yang Guangyuan incited the Khitan and war broke out at Chanyuan. Every order for confronting the enemy came from Yanguang; Weihan and the other chief ministers had no share in it.

sentences.zh: 及戎王退，維翰使親黨受寵於少帝者，密致自薦，曰：「陛下欲制北方以安天下，非維翰不可。

translations.literal: When the Khitan ruler withdrew, Weihan had a close associate favored by the Young Emperor secretly recommend himself, saying: "If Your Majesty wishes to control the north and settle the realm, no one but Weihan will do.
translations.idiomatic: After the Khitan ruler withdrew, Weihan had a trusted ally in the Young Emperor's favor secretly recommend him, saying, "If Your Majesty means to master the north and secure the realm, none but Weihan can do it.

sentences.zh: 」少帝乃出延廣守洛，以維翰守中書令，再為樞密使、宏文館大學士，繼封魏國公。

translations.literal: " The Young Emperor then sent Yanguang out to guard Luoyang, made Weihan Director of the Secretariat, again appointed him Commissioner of Military Affairs and Grand Academician of the Hall of Illustrious Culture, and enfeoffed him Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: " The Young Emperor then posted Jing Yanguang to guard Luoyang, made Weihan Director of the Secretariat, restored him as Commissioner of Military Affairs and Grand Academician of the Hall of Illustrious Culture, and enfeoffed him Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 事無巨細，一以委之。

translations.literal: Whether the matter was great or small, all was entrusted to him alone.
translations.idiomatic: Great affairs and small alike were left entirely to him.

sentences.zh: 數月之間，百度浸理。

translations.literal: Within a few months, the hundred offices were gradually brought into order.
translations.idiomatic: Within months, government was gradually set right.

sentences.zh: 然權位既重，而四方賂遺，鹹湊其門，故仍歲之間，積貨鉅萬，由是澆競輩得以興謗。

translations.literal: Yet as his power and position grew weighty, bribes and gifts from all quarters piled at his gate; thus within a year he amassed goods worth tens of thousands, and by this the corrupt and competitive crowd were able to stir up slander.
translations.idiomatic: But power brought weight, and gifts from every quarter flooded his gate. Within a year he had amassed a fortune worth tens of thousands, giving the greedy and ambitious room to spread slander against him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，內客省使李彥韜、端明殿學士馮玉皆以親舊用事，與維翰不協，間言稍入。

translations.literal: Before long, the Inner Guests Bureau envoy Li Yantao and Hall of Brilliant Clarity academician Feng Yu both used kin and old associates in office; they were at odds with Weihan, and whispered words gradually reached the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Yantao, envoy of the Inner Guests Bureau, and Feng Yu, academician of the Hall of Brilliant Clarity, both staffed the court with kin and cronies. At odds with Weihan, they began feeding the emperor private words against him.

sentences.zh: 維翰漸見疏忌，將加黜退，賴宰相劉昫李崧奏云：「維翰元勛，且無顯過，不宜輕有進退。

translations.literal: Weihan was gradually seen as distant and distrusted; demotion was about to be imposed, but thanks to the memorial of chancellors Liu Xu and Li Song, who said: "Weihan is an original meritorious minister and has no obvious fault; he should not be lightly promoted or dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Weihan was gradually sidelined and suspected; dismissal was imminent until chancellors Liu Xu and Li Song memorialized: "Weihan is a founding minister without any clear fault. He should not be lightly removed.

sentences.zh: 」少帝乃止。

translations.literal: " The Young Emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The Young Emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 尋以馮玉為樞密使，以分維翰之權。

translations.literal: Soon Feng Yu was made Commissioner of Military Affairs to divide Weihan's authority.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Feng Yu was made Commissioner of Military Affairs to split Weihan's power.

sentences.zh: 後因少帝微有不豫，維翰曾密遣中使達意於太后，請為皇弟重睿擇師傅以教道之，少帝以此疑其有他。

translations.literal: Later, because the Young Emperor was slightly unwell, Weihan had once secretly sent a palace envoy to convey his intent to the Empress Dowager, asking that tutors be chosen for the imperial younger brother Chongrui to instruct and guide him; the Young Emperor for this reason suspected he had other designs.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Young Emperor fell briefly ill, Weihan had secretly sent a palace envoy to the Empress Dowager asking that tutors be chosen for his younger brother Chongrui. The Young Emperor took this as a sign of hidden ambition.

sentences.zh: 俄而馮玉作相，與維翰同在中書，會舍人盧價秩滿，玉乃下筆除價為工部侍郎，維翰曰：「詞臣除此官稍慢，恐外有所議。

translations.literal: Before long Feng Yu became chancellor and served with Weihan in the Secretariat; when Academician-Secretary Lu Jia's term expired, Yu drafted an appointment making Jia Vice Minister of Works. Weihan said: "For a literary official this appointment is rather slow; I fear there will be outside criticism.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Feng Yu became chancellor and shared the Secretariat with Weihan. When Academician-Secretary Lu Jia's term expired, Yu drafted an order appointing him Vice Minister of Works. Weihan said, "For a drafting official this promotion is rather slow. Outsiders will surely talk.

sentences.zh: 」因不署名，屬維翰休假，玉竟除之，自此維翰與玉尤不相協。

translations.literal: " Therefore he did not sign; while Weihan was on leave, Yu went ahead and issued the appointment, and from this time Weihan and Yu were especially at odds.
translations.idiomatic: " He refused to sign. While Weihan was on leave, Yu issued the appointment anyway, and from then on the two men were bitterly opposed.

sentences.zh: 俄因少帝以重睿擇師傅言於玉，玉遂以詞激少帝，尋出維翰為開封府尹。

translations.literal: Before long, because the Young Emperor spoke to Yu about choosing tutors for Chongrui, Yu inflamed the Young Emperor with sharp words, and soon Weihan was sent out as Intendant of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Young Emperor mentioned the tutor affair to Feng Yu, who goaded him with inflammatory words. Weihan was promptly sent out as Intendant of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 維翰稱足疾，罕預朝謁，不接賓客。

translations.literal: Weihan claimed foot ailment, rarely attended court audiences, and received no guests.
translations.idiomatic: Weihan pleaded foot trouble, rarely appeared at court, and refused visitors.

sentences.zh: 是歲，秋霖經月不歇。

translations.literal: That year autumn rains fell month after month without cease.
translations.idiomatic: That year the autumn rains lasted a full month without stopping.

sentences.zh: 一日，維翰出府門由西街入內，至國子門，馬忽驚逸，禦者不能制，維翰落水，久而方蘇。

translations.literal: One day Weihan left the prefectural gate, entered the palace by the west street, and at the Guozi Gate his horse suddenly bolted in panic; the driver could not control it, Weihan fell into the water, and only after a long while did he revive.
translations.idiomatic: One day Weihan left his office, entered the palace by the west street, and at the Guozi Gate his horse suddenly panicked and bolted. The groom could not hold it; Weihan fell into the water and was a long time coming to.

sentences.zh: 或言私邸亦多怪異，親黨鹹憂之。

translations.literal: Some said his private residence too had many strange occurrences, and kin and followers were all troubled.
translations.idiomatic: Some said his private house was also haunted by strange things, and his kin and followers were deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 及契丹至中渡橋，維翰以國家安危系在朝夕，乃詣執政異其議，又求見帝，復不得對。

translations.literal: When the Khitan reached Zhongdu Bridge, Weihan, feeling the state's safety and peril hung on the day and hour, went to the chief ministers to differ with their counsel, and again sought audience with the emperor, but still could not be received.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan reached Zhongdu Bridge, Weihan saw the state's survival hanging by a thread. He went to the chief ministers to dispute their policy and again begged audience with the emperor, but was still refused.

sentences.zh: 維翰退而謂所親曰：「若以社稷之靈，天命未改，非所能知也；

translations.literal: Weihan withdrew and told those close to him: "If by the spirit of the altars of state Heaven's mandate has not changed, that is not something we can know;
translations.idiomatic: Weihan withdrew and told those close to him, "If the altars of state still have their guardian spirit and Heaven's mandate has not shifted, that is beyond us to know;

sentences.zh: 若以人事言之，晉氏將不血食矣。」

translations.literal: but if we speak of human affairs, the house of Jin will soon cease to receive sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: but if we judge by what men do, the house of Jin will soon cease to receive sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 開運三年十二月十日，王師既降契丹；

translations.literal: On the tenth day of the twelfth month of the third year of Kaiyun, the royal army had already surrendered to the Khitan;
translations.idiomatic: On the tenth day of the twelfth month of the third year of Kaiyun, the imperial army had already surrendered to the Khitan;

sentences.zh: 十六日，張彥澤以前鋒騎軍陷都城。

translations.literal: on the sixteenth Zhang Yanze, with the vanguard cavalry, stormed the capital.
translations.idiomatic: on the sixteenth Zhang Yanze led the vanguard cavalry and broke into the capital.

sentences.zh: 戎王遣使遺太后書云：「可先使桑維翰、景延廣遠來相接，甚是好事。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler sent an envoy with a letter to the Empress Dowager saying: "You may first send Sang Weihan and Jing Yanguang from afar to meet us; that would be a very good thing.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler sent the Empress Dowager a letter saying, "Send Sang Weihan and Jing Yanguang from afar to meet us first. That would be an excellent move.

sentences.zh: 」是日淩旦，都下軍亂，宮中火發。

translations.literal: " At dawn that day the capital fell into military disorder and fire broke out in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: " At dawn that day the capital erupted in mutiny and fire broke out in the palace.

sentences.zh: 維翰時在府署，左右勸使逃避，維翰曰：「吾國家大臣，何所逃乎！

translations.literal: Weihan was then in his office; those around him urged him to flee. Weihan said: "I am a great minister of the state—where would I flee?
translations.idiomatic: Weihan was in his office. Those around him urged him to run. He said, "I am a minister of this state. Where would I go?

sentences.zh: 」即坐以俟命。

translations.literal: " He simply sat and waited for orders.
translations.idiomatic: " He sat where he was and waited for his fate.

sentences.zh: 時少帝已受戎王撫慰之命，乃謀自全之計，因思維翰在相時，累貢謀畫，請與契丹和，慮戎王到京窮究其事，則顯彰己過，故欲殺維翰以滅其口，因令圖之。

translations.literal: At that time the Young Emperor had already received the Khitan ruler's command of reassurance and plotted a plan to save himself; he recalled that while Weihan was chancellor he had repeatedly submitted plans urging peace with the Khitan, and feared that when the Khitan ruler reached the capital and thoroughly investigated the matter his own fault would stand exposed; therefore he wished to kill Weihan to silence him, and ordered it plotted.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Young Emperor had accepted the Khitan ruler's reassurance and was scheming to save himself. He remembered that as chancellor Weihan had repeatedly urged peace with the Khitan, and feared that once the Khitan reached the capital and traced the matter, his own guilt would stand exposed. He decided to kill Weihan to seal his lips and gave orders to that effect.

sentences.zh: 張彥澤既受少帝密旨，復利維翰家財，乃稱少帝命召維翰。

translations.literal: Zhang Yanze, having received the Young Emperor's secret order and coveting Weihan's family wealth besides, claimed the Young Emperor's command and summoned Weihan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanze, acting on the Young Emperor's secret order and eager for Weihan's family wealth, summoned him in the emperor's name.

sentences.zh: 維翰束帶乘馬，行及天街，與李崧相遇，交談之次，有軍吏於馬前揖維翰赴侍衛司，維翰知其不可，顧謂崧曰：「侍中當國，今日國亡，翻令維翰死之，何也？

translations.literal: Weihan girded himself and mounted; when he reached the Celestial Street he met Li Song. As they spoke, a military clerk came before his horse and bowed Weihan toward the Palace Guard office. Weihan knew it was hopeless and, turning to Song, said: "As Vice Grand Counselor you hold the state; today the state is perishing, yet you would have Weihan die for it—why?
translations.idiomatic: Weihan dressed formally and rode out. On the Celestial Street he met Li Song. As they talked, a military clerk came before his horse and bowed him toward the Palace Guard office. Weihan knew what awaited him and turned to Song: "You hold the reins of state as Palace Attendant. The realm falls today, and you would have me die for it—why?

sentences.zh: 」崧甚有愧色。

translations.literal: " Song was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: " Song flushed with shame.

sentences.zh: 是日，彥澤遣兵守之，十八日夜，為彥澤所害，時年四十九。

translations.literal: That day Yanze sent soldiers to guard him; on the night of the eighteenth he was killed by Yanze. He was forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: That day Yanze posted guards over him. On the night of the eighteenth Yanze killed him. He was forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 即以衣帶加頸，報戎王主：維翰自經而死。

translations.literal: They placed a sash about his neck and reported to the Khitan ruler: Weihan had hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: They looped a sash around his neck and reported to the Khitan ruler that Weihan had hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 戎王主曰：「我本無心害維翰，維翰不合自致。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler said: "I never meant to harm Weihan; Weihan should not have brought this on himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler said, "I never meant to harm Weihan. He brought this on himself.

sentences.zh: 」戎王至闕，使人驗其狀，令殯於私第，厚撫其家，所有田園邸第，並令賜之。

translations.literal: " When the Khitan ruler reached the palace he sent men to verify the circumstances, ordered the body laid out at his private residence, treated the family generously, and commanded that all his fields, gardens, mansions, and estates be granted to them.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Khitan ruler reached the palace he sent men to verify what had happened, ordered the body laid out at Weihan's private residence, treated the family generously, and granted them all his fields, gardens, and mansions.

sentences.zh: 及漢高祖登極，詔贈尚書令。

translations.literal: When Gaozu of Han ascended the throne, an edict posthumously appointed him Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu of Han took the throne, an edict posthumously made him Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 維翰少時所居，恒有魑魅，家人鹹畏之，維翰往往被竊其衣，撮其巾櫛，而未嘗改容。

translations.literal: In the place where Weihan lived in youth there were always demons and sprites; his family all feared them. Weihan would often have his clothes stolen and his caps and combs snatched away, yet he never changed expression.
translations.idiomatic: The house where Weihan lived as a youth was haunted; his family all feared it. Spirits would steal his clothes and snatch his caps and combs, yet he never so much as changed expression.

sentences.zh: 當兩朝秉政，出上將楊光遠、景延廣俱為洛川守；

translations.literal: While wielding power under two reigns, he sent out the great generals Yang Guangyuan and Jing Yanguang, both as governors of Luoyang;
translations.idiomatic: While he held power under two reigns, he posted the great generals Yang Guangyuan and Jing Yanguang as governors of Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 又嘗一制除節將十五人，各領軍職，無不屈而服之。

translations.literal: he also once in a single edict appointed fifteen military commissioners, each with army command, and none failed to submit and obey.
translations.idiomatic: and once issued a single edict appointing fifteen military commissioners to army commands, every one of whom bowed and obeyed.

sentences.zh: 理安陽除民弊二十餘事，在兗、海擒豪賊過千人，亦寇恂、尹翁歸之流也。

translations.literal: He governed Anyang and cleared away more than twenty abuses burdening the people; in Yan and Hai he captured over a thousand powerful bandits—truly a man in the mold of Kou Xun and Yin Wenggui.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Anyang and removed more than twenty burdens on the people; in Yan and Hai he captured over a thousand powerful bandits—a man in the line of Kou Xun and Yin Wenggui.

sentences.zh: 開運中，朝廷以長子坦為屯田員外郎，次子塤為秘書郎。

translations.literal: During Kaiyun the court appointed his eldest son Tan as Vice Director of the Directorate for State Farms and his second son Xun as Secretary of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyun the court appointed his eldest son Tan Vice Director of the Directorate for State Farms and his second son Xun Secretary of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 維翰謂同列曰：「漢代三公之子為郎，廢已久矣，近或行之，甚喧外議。

translations.literal: Weihan told his colleagues: "In Han times the sons of the Three Ducal Ministers served as gentlemen-attendants; the custom has long been abandoned. Lately it has sometimes been revived, and outside criticism has been loud.
translations.idiomatic: Weihan told his colleagues, "In Han times the sons of the Three Ducal Ministers served as gentlemen-attendants—a custom long dead. Reviving it now has stirred loud public criticism.

sentences.zh: 」乃抗表固讓不受。

translations.literal: " He then submitted a strongly worded memorial firmly declining to accept.
translations.idiomatic: " He submitted a forceful memorial firmly refusing the appointments.

sentences.zh: 尋改坦為大理司直，塤為秘書省正字，議者美之。

translations.literal: Soon Tan was changed to Registrar of the Court of Judicial Review and Xun to Proofreader in the Secretariat, and commentators praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Tan was reassigned Registrar of the Court of Judicial Review and Xun Proofreader in the Secretariat, a change commentators praised.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖在位時，詔廢翰林學士院，由是並內外制皆歸閣下，命舍人直內廷，數年之間，尤重其選。

translations.literal: Early on, while Gaozu held the throne, an edict abolished the Hanlin Academy; thereafter both inner and outer edicts were handled under the Secretariat, palace secretaries were posted to the inner court, and for several years their selection was held in especial esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Gaozu's reign an edict abolished the Hanlin Academy, so that inner and outer edicts alike passed through the Secretariat. Palace secretaries were posted to the inner court, and for years their selection was held in high regard.

sentences.zh: 及維翰再居宥密，不信宿，奏復置學士院，凡署職者，皆其親舊。

translations.literal: When Weihan again occupied the privy council he had little faith in the long-standing arrangement and memorialized to restore the Hanlin Academy; all who received appointments were his kin and old associates.
translations.idiomatic: When Weihan returned to the privy council he distrusted the established order and memorialized to restore the Hanlin Academy, filling every post with kin and old associates.

sentences.zh: 時議者以維翰相業素高，公望所屬，雖除授或黨，亦弗之咎也。

translations.literal: Contemporary commentators held that Weihan's ministerial achievement had always been lofty and the public look was upon him; though some appointments showed factional favor, none blamed him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators of the day held that Weihan's ministerial stature was high and the public looked to him; though some appointments favored his own circle, none held it against him.

sentences.zh: （《五代史補》：桑維翰形貌甚怪，往往見之者失次。

translations.literal: (The Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: Sang Weihan's appearance was very strange; those who saw him were often disconcerted.
translations.idiomatic: (The Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties records that Sang Weihan's appearance was so strange that those who met him were often thrown off balance.

sentences.zh: 張彥澤素以驍勇稱，每謁候，雖冬月未嘗不雨汗。

translations.literal: Zhang Yanze was famed for fierce courage; whenever he called to pay respects, even in winter months he never failed to break into a sweat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanze was known for fierce bravery; whenever he came to call, even in midwinter he broke out in a sweat.

sentences.zh: 及中渡變生，彥澤引蕃部至，欲逞其威，乃領眾突入開封府，弓矢亂發，且問：「桑維翰安在？

translations.literal: When crisis struck at Zhongdu Bridge, Yanze brought Khitan forces in and, wanting to show his might, led his men in a sudden rush into the Kaifeng prefectural office, arrows flying wildly, and demanded: "Where is Sang Weihan?
translations.idiomatic: When disaster struck at Zhongdu Bridge, Yanze brought Khitan troops into the city to strut his power. He led his men in a sudden charge on the Kaifeng prefectural office, arrows flying everywhere, shouting, "Where is Sang Weihan?

sentences.zh: 」維翰聞之，乃厲聲曰：「吾為大臣，使國家如此，其死宜矣。

translations.literal: " Weihan heard this and shouted in a stern voice: "I am a great minister and have brought the state to this pass; my death is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: " Weihan heard him and cried out in a thunderous voice, "I am a great minister who has brought the state to ruin. Death is what I deserve.

sentences.zh: 張彥澤安得無禮！

translations.literal: Zhang Yanze, how dare you show such disrespect!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanze, how dare you treat me with such insolence!

sentences.zh: 」乃升廳安坐數之曰：「汝有何功，帶使相已臨方面，當國家危急，不能盡犬馬之力以為報效，一旦背叛，助契丹作威為賊，汝心安乎？

translations.literal: " He then mounted the hall, sat composed, and rebuked him: "What merit have you? Granted the title of envoy-minister and already commanding a region—when the state was in peril you could not exhaust yourself in loyal service. Then in a single day you turned traitor and helped the Khitan vaunt their power like brigands. Does your heart rest easy?
translations.idiomatic: " He mounted the hall, sat calmly, and rebuked him: "What have you ever done? You hold the rank of envoy-minister and command a region, yet when the state was in peril you gave no loyal service. Then overnight you turned traitor and helped the Khitan play the tyrant like common bandits. Can you live with that?

sentences.zh: 」彥澤睹其詞氣慨然，股粟不敢仰視，退曰：「吾不知桑維翰何人，今日之下，威棱猶如此，其再可見耶！

translations.literal: " Yanze saw his words and bearing so forceful that his legs trembled and he dared not look up; withdrawing he said: "I never knew what sort of man Sang Weihan was—brought low today, his awful presence is still such as this. How could one bear to see him again!
translations.idiomatic: " Yanze, struck by his force of word and bearing, trembled in the legs and dared not meet his eyes. He withdrew saying, "I never knew what kind of man Sang Weihan was. Brought this low, his authority is still terrifying. Who could bear to face him again?

sentences.zh: 」是夜，令壯士就府縊殺之。

translations.literal: " That night he ordered braves to go to the office and strangle him to death.
translations.idiomatic: " That night he sent strongmen to the prefectural office to strangle him.

sentences.zh: 當維翰之縊也，猶瞋目直視，噓其氣再三，每一噓皆有火出，其光赫然，三噓之外，火盡滅，就視則奄然矣。）〉

translations.literal: When Weihan was being strangled, his eyes were still wide and staring straight ahead. He exhaled three times, and with each breath fire issued forth, its light blazing bright. After the third breath the fire was wholly extinguished; when they went to look, he was already still.)〉
translations.idiomatic: As Weihan was being strangled, his eyes remained wide and fixed. He exhaled three times, and with each breath fire burst forth, blazing bright. After the third breath the fire died away; when they looked again, he was gone.)]

sentences.zh: 趙瑩，字元輝，華陰人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Ying, styled Yuanhui, was a native of Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ying, whose style was Yuanhui, came from Huayin.

sentences.zh: 曾祖溥，江陵縣丞。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Pu served as assistant magistrate of Jiangling County.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Pu was assistant magistrate of Jiangling County.

sentences.zh: 祖孺，秘書正字。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ru was a proofreader in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ru was a proofreader in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父居晦，為農。

translations.literal: His father Juhui was a farmer.
translations.idiomatic: His father Juhui was a farmer.

sentences.zh: 瑩風儀美秀，性復純謹。

translations.literal: Ying's bearing was graceful and handsome, and his nature moreover pure and careful.
translations.idiomatic: Ying had a handsome and refined bearing, and a nature that was pure and careful.

sentences.zh: 梁龍德中，始解褐為康延孝從事。

translations.literal: In the Longde era of Later Liang he first left the commoner's robe to serve as staff officer to Kang Yanxiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the Longde era of Later Liang he first entered official service as staff officer to Kang Yanxiao.

sentences.zh: 後唐同光中，延孝鎮陜州，會莊宗伐蜀，命延孝為騎將。

translations.literal: During the Tongguang era of Later Tang, Yanxiao was stationed at Shazhou; when Emperor Zhuangzong campaigned against Shu he was ordered to serve as cavalry commander.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tongguang era of Later Tang, Yanxiao was posted to Shazhou. When Emperor Zhuangzong marched against Shu, he was made cavalry commander.

sentences.zh: 將行，留瑩監修金天神祠。

translations.literal: Before departing, he left Ying in charge of rebuilding the Golden Heaven Spirit Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Before he set out, he left Ying in charge of rebuilding the Golden Heaven Spirit Temple.

sentences.zh: 功既集，忽夢神召於前亭，待以優禮，謂瑩曰：「公富有前程，所宜自愛。

translations.literal: When the work was completed, Ying suddenly dreamed the spirit summoned him to the front pavilion and received him with distinguished courtesy, saying: "Sir, you have a bountiful future ahead; you should take good care of yourself.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, Ying dreamed that the spirit summoned him to the front pavilion and received him with great honor, saying, "You have a bright future ahead. Take good care of yourself.

sentences.zh: 」因遺一劍一笏，覺而駭異。

translations.literal: " He then bestowed a sword and a tablet; when Ying awoke he was startled and amazed.
translations.idiomatic: " Then the spirit gave him a sword and a court tablet. When Ying woke, he was shaken and astonished.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，以高祖為陜府兩使留後，瑩時在郡，以前官謁之，一見如舊相識，即奏署管記。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, Gaozu was made military governor of Shaanxi with dual commission and remained in post. Ying was then in the prefecture; he paid his respects in his former office, and at one meeting they were like old acquaintances. He immediately memorialized and appointed him secretary in charge of records.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, Gaozu was appointed military governor of Shaanxi with dual commission and remained in office. Ying was then serving in the prefecture; he called on him under his former title, and at their first meeting they felt like old friends. Gaozu at once had him appointed chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 高祖歷諸鎮皆從之，累使闕下，官至御史大夫，賜金紫。

translations.literal: As Gaozu served at the various military posts, Ying followed him everywhere. He was sent to the capital repeatedly and rose to Censor-in-Chief, receiving the gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Gaozu was posted, Ying went with him. He was sent to court again and again, rose to Censor-in-Chief, and was granted the gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 高祖再鎮并州，位至節度判官。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was again made military governor of Bingzhou, Ying rose to the rank of military governor's adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu returned to command at Bingzhou, Ying was promoted to adjutant of the military governorship.

sentences.zh: 高祖建號，授瑩翰林學士承旨、金紫光祿大夫、戶部侍郎，知太原府事，尋遷門下侍郎、同平章事、監修國史。

translations.literal: When Gaozu established his imperial title, Ying was appointed Hanlin Academician in Charge, Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Girdle, and Vice Minister of Revenue, and given charge of Taiyuan prefecture affairs. Soon after he was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery, Junior Grand Councilor, and Supervisor of the Compilation of National History.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu proclaimed his dynasty, Ying was made Hanlin Academician in Charge, Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Girdle, and Vice Minister of Revenue, with charge of Taiyuan. He was soon promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery, Junior Grand Councilor, and Supervisor of the Compilation of National History.

sentences.zh: 車駕入洛，使持聘謝契丹，及還，加光祿大夫兼吏部尚書，判戶部。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage entered Luoyang, Ying was dispatched to carry tribute and offer thanks to the Khitan. Upon his return he was further appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and concurrently Minister of Personnel, with charge over the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor entered Luoyang, Ying was sent to carry tribute and offer thanks to the Khitan. On his return he was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and concurrently Minister of Personnel, with charge of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 初，瑩為從事，丁母憂，高祖不許歸華下，以粗缞隨幕，人或短之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ying was a staff officer, his mother died and he entered mourning. Gaozu would not permit him to return to Huayin and had him follow the staff in coarse hemp mourning garb. Some spoke ill of this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Ying was serving on staff, his mother died and he entered mourning. Gaozu would not let him return to Huayin and required him to remain with the staff in coarse mourning dress. Some criticized this.

sentences.zh: 及入相，以敦讓汲引為務。

translations.literal: Once he entered the chancellorship, he made it his business to promote men through sincerity and humility.
translations.idiomatic: Once he became chancellor, he devoted himself to advancing others through sincerity and modesty.

sentences.zh: 監修國史日，以唐代故事殘缺，署能者居職，纂補實錄及修正史二百卷行於時，瑩首有力焉。

translations.literal: While supervising the compilation of national history, finding that Tang-era records and precedents were fragmentary, he appointed capable men to their posts and compiled and supplemented the Veritable Records and Corrected History in two hundred scrolls that circulated at the time. Ying was first and foremost among those who made this possible.
translations.idiomatic: As supervisor of the national history, he found Tang records and precedents badly incomplete. He placed capable men in the posts and compiled and supplemented the Veritable Records and Corrected History in two hundred scrolls that circulated at the time. Ying was chiefly responsible for this achievement.

sentences.zh: 少帝嗣位，拜守中書令。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded to the throne, Ying was appointed Acting Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor succeeded to the throne, Ying was appointed Acting Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年，檢校太尉本官，出為晉昌軍節度使。

translations.literal: The following year he was made Acting Grand General while retaining his existing rank, and sent out as military governor of Jinchang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made Acting Grand General while keeping his existing rank and sent out as military governor of Jinchang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 是時，天下大蝗，境內捕蝗者獲蝗一斗，給粟一斗，使饑者獲濟，遠近嘉之。

translations.literal: At that time locusts ravaged the empire. Within his jurisdiction he gave one peck of grain for each peck of locusts collected, so that the hungry could be relieved. People near and far praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts then ravaged the empire. In his circuit he offered one peck of grain for every peck of locusts collected, relieving the hungry. People near and far praised the policy.

sentences.zh: 未幾，移鎮華州，歲餘入為開封尹。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Huazhou; after a little over a year he was recalled to serve as Intendant of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Huazhou, and after a little more than a year was recalled to serve as Intendant of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 開運末，馮玉、李彥韜用事，以桑維翰才望素重，而瑩柔而可制，因共稱之，乃出維翰，復瑩相位，加宏文館大學士。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaiyun era, Feng Yu and Li Yantao held power. Because Sang Weihan's talent and prestige had long been weighty while Ying was pliant and could be controlled, they jointly praised Ying. Weihan was removed and Ying was restored to the chancellorship, with the additional title of Grand Academician of the Hall of Expansive Literature.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kaiyun era, Feng Yu and Li Yantao held power. Sang Weihan's talent and prestige had long been great, but Ying was mild and manageable, so they praised him together. Weihan was removed and Ying was restored to the chancellorship, with the added title of Grand Academician of the Hall of Expansive Literature.

sentences.zh: 及李崧、馮玉議出兵應接趙延壽，而以杜重威為都督部署，瑩私謂馮、李曰：「杜中令國之懿親，所求未愜，心恒怏怏，安可更與兵權？

translations.literal: When Li Song and Feng Yu discussed dispatching troops to support Zhao Yanshou and made Du Chongwei overall commander, Ying privately said to Feng and Li: "Vice Director Du is the state's close imperial kinsman. His requests have not been satisfied and his heart has long been sullen. How can we further entrust him with military authority?
translations.idiomatic: When Li Song and Feng Yu debated sending troops to support Zhao Yanshou and made Du Chongwei overall commander, Ying said privately to Feng and Li, "Vice Director Du is a close imperial kinsman of the state. His wishes have not been granted and he has long brooded in discontent. How can we give him military authority again?

sentences.zh: 若有事邊陲，只李守貞將之可也。

translations.literal: If there is trouble on the frontier, Li Shouzhen alone should be put in command."
translations.idiomatic: If there is trouble on the frontier, Li Shouzhen alone should lead the army."

sentences.zh: 」及契丹陷京城，契丹主遷少帝於北塞，瑩與馮玉、李彥韜俱從。

translations.literal: " When the Khitan took the capital, the Khitan ruler moved the Young Emperor to the northern borderlands. Ying followed together with Feng Yu and Li Yantao.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Khitan took the capital, the Khitan ruler moved the Young Emperor to the northern frontier. Ying followed together with Feng Yu and Li Yantao.
