sentences.zh: 契丹永康王代立，授瑩太子太保。

translations.literal: When the Khitan Prince of Yongkang succeeded to the throne, he appointed Ying Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan Prince of Yongkang succeeded to the throne, he appointed Ying Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，遣尚書左丞田敏報命於契丹，遇瑩於幽州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhou Guangshun era, Tian Min, Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, was sent to report to the Khitan. He encountered Ying at Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhou Guangshun era, Tian Min, Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, was sent to report to the Khitan and encountered Ying at Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 瑩得見華人，悲悵不已，謂田敏曰：「老身漂零寄於此，近聞室家喪逝，弱子無恙，蒙中朝皇帝倍加存恤，東京舊第本屬公家，亦聞優恩特給善價，老夫至死無以報效。

translations.literal: On meeting Chinese people, Ying could not stop his grief and sorrow. He said to Tian Min: "This old body drifts in exile here. I have lately heard that my wife and family have died. My young son remains unharmed. I am deeply grateful that the emperor of the Middle Court has shown me special care. Our old residence in the Eastern Capital originally belonged to the state, and I have also heard that by special favor a fair price was granted. To my dying day I shall have no way to repay such kindness.
translations.idiomatic: On seeing fellow Chinese, Ying was overcome with grief. He told Tian Min, "This old man drifts in exile here. I have lately heard that my wife and family are dead. My young son is unharmed, and I am deeply grateful that the emperor of the Middle Court has shown me special kindness. Our old residence in the Eastern Capital originally belonged to the state, and I have heard that by special favor a fair price was granted. To my dying day I shall have no way to repay it.

sentences.zh: 」於是南望稽首，涕泗橫流。

translations.literal: " At this he bowed toward the south, tears streaming down his face.
translations.idiomatic: " He then bowed toward the south, tears streaming down his face.

sentences.zh: 先是，漢高祖以入蕃將相第宅遍賜隨駕大臣，故以瑩第賜周太祖。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Han Emperor Gaozu had distributed the mansions of generals and ministers who entered the barbarian realm among the ministers who followed the imperial carriage. Thus Ying's mansion was granted to the Zhou Emperor Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Han Gaozu had distributed the mansions of generals and ministers who had entered the Khitan realm among the ministers who followed the imperial carriage. Ying's mansion was therefore granted to Zhou Taizu.

sentences.zh: 太祖時為樞密副使，召瑩子前刑部郎中易則告之曰：「所賜第，除素屬版籍外，如有別契券為己所置者，可歸本直。

translations.literal: At the time Taizu was Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs. He summoned Ying's son, the former Director of the Ministry of Justice Yize, and told him: "Of the mansion granted, apart from what has long been on the official register, if there are separate deeds for property you yourselves acquired, you may recover the original cost.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Taizu was Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs. He summoned Ying's son, the former Director of the Ministry of Justice Yize, and told him, "Of the mansion granted, apart from what has long been on the official register, if there are separate deeds for property your family acquired, you may recover the original cost.

sentences.zh: 」即以千餘緡遺易則。

translations.literal: " He thereupon gave Yize more than a thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: " He then gave Yize more than a thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 易則惶恐辭讓，周太祖堅與之方受，故瑩言及之。

translations.literal: Yize fearfully declined, but only after Zhou Taizu insisted did he accept. This is why Ying spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: Yize fearfully declined, but only after Zhou Taizu insisted did he accept. This is why Ying mentioned it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，瑩卒於幽州，時年六十七。

translations.literal: Before long Ying died at Youzhou. He was sixty-seven years old.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Ying died at Youzhou, aged sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 瑩初被疾，遣人祈告於契丹主，願歸骨於南朝，使羈魂幸復鄉里，契丹主閔而許之。

translations.literal: When Ying first fell ill, he sent someone to pray to the Khitan ruler, asking that his bones be returned to the Southern Court so that his captive soul might at last reach home again. The Khitan ruler took pity and granted this.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying first fell ill, he sent someone to pray to the Khitan ruler, asking that his bones be returned to the Southern Court so that his captive soul might at last reach home. The Khitan ruler took pity and granted the request.

sentences.zh: 及卒，遣其子易從、家人數輩護喪而還，仍遣大將送至京師。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Yicong and several members of the household escorted the coffin back. A great general was also sent to convey them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his son Yicong and several members of the household escorted the coffin back, and a great general was sent to convey them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 周太祖感嘆久之，詔贈太傅，仍賜其子絹五百匹，以備喪事，令歸葬於華陰故裏。

translations.literal: Zhou Taizu sighed for a long time and issued an edict posthumously appointing him Grand Tutor. He also granted his son five hundred bolts of silk for funeral expenses and ordered that he be buried in his old home at Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Taizu sighed for a long time and issued an edict posthumously appointing him Grand Tutor. He also granted his son five hundred bolts of silk for the funeral and ordered burial in his old home at Huayin.

sentences.zh: 劉昫，字耀遠，涿州歸義人也。

translations.literal: Liu Xu, styled Yaoyuan, was a native of Guiyi in Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xu, whose style was Yaoyuan, came from Guiyi in Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 祖乘，幽府左司馬；

translations.literal: His grandfather Cheng was Left Army Supervisor of the Youzhou prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Cheng was Left Army Supervisor of the Youzhou prefecture;

sentences.zh: 父因，幽州巡官。

translations.literal: his father Yin was an inspector of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: his father Yin was an inspector of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 昫神彩秀拔，文學優贍，與兄晅、弟皞，俱有鄉曲之譽。

translations.literal: Xu's spirit and appearance were outstanding and refined, and his literary learning abundant. He and his elder brother Xuan and younger brother Hao all enjoyed local fame.
translations.idiomatic: Xu had an outstanding and refined bearing and abundant literary learning. He and his elder brother Xuan and younger brother Hao all enjoyed local renown.

sentences.zh: 唐天佑中，契丹陷其郡，昫被俘至新州，逃而獲免。

translations.literal: During the Tianyou era of Tang, when the Khitan took his prefecture, Xu was captured and taken to Xinzhou. He escaped and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tang Tianyou era, when the Khitan took his prefecture, Xu was captured and taken to Xinzhou. He escaped and survived.

sentences.zh: 後居上國大寧山，與呂夢奇、張麟結庵共處，以吟誦自娛。

translations.literal: Later he lived on Mount Daning in the Upper Country, building a hut together with Lu Mengqi and Zhang Lin and amusing themselves with recitation.
translations.idiomatic: Later he lived on Mount Daning in the Upper Country, building a hut with Lu Mengqi and Zhang Lin and amusing themselves with recitation.

sentences.zh: 會定州連帥王處直以其子都為易州刺史，署昫為軍事衙推。

translations.literal: When Wang Chuzhi, military commissioner of Dingzhou, appointed his son Du prefect of Yizhou, Xu was made military record officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chuzhi, military commissioner of Dingzhou, appointed his son Du prefect of Yizhou, Xu was made military record officer.

sentences.zh: 及都去任，乞假還鄉，都招昫至中山。

translations.literal: When Du left his post, Xu asked leave to return home. Du summoned Xu to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: When Du left his post, Xu asked leave to return home. Du summoned Xu to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 會其兄晅自本郡至，都薦於其父，尋署為節度衙推，不逾歲，命為觀察推官。

translations.literal: When his elder brother Xuan arrived from their home prefecture, Du recommended Xu to his father. Soon Xu was appointed military record officer of the circuit; before a year had passed he was made surveillance commissioner staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother Xuan arrived from their home prefecture, Du recommended Xu to his father. Xu was soon appointed military record officer of the circuit, and before a year had passed was made surveillance commissioner staff officer.

sentences.zh: 歷二年，都篡父位。

translations.literal: After two years Du usurped his father's position.
translations.idiomatic: After two years Du usurped his father's position.

sentences.zh: 時都有客和少微素嫉亙，構而殺之，昫越境而去，寓居浮陽，節度使李存審辟為從事。

translations.literal: At the time Du had a retainer named He Shaowei who had long envied Geng. He framed him and had him killed. Xu crossed the border and left, taking residence at Fuyang, where the military governor Li Cunshen recruited him as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Du had a retainer named He Shaowei who had long envied Geng. He framed Geng and had him killed. Xu fled across the border and settled at Fuyang, where the military governor Li Cunshen recruited him as staff officer.

sentences.zh: 莊宗即位，授太常博士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong took the throne, Xu was appointed Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong took the throne, Xu was appointed Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 尋擢為翰林學士，繼改膳部員外郎，賜緋；

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Hanlin Academician, then transferred to Vice Director of the Board of Provisions and given scarlet robes;
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Hanlin Academician, then transferred to Vice Director of the Board of Provisions and granted scarlet robes;

sentences.zh: 比部郎中，賜紫。

translations.literal: and then Director of the Board of Review, given purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: then Director of the Board of Review, granted purple robes.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服闋，授庫部郎中，依舊充職。

translations.literal: When his mother died he entered mourning. After mourning ended he was appointed Director of the Board of Stores and continued in his former Hanlin post.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he entered mourning. After mourning ended he was appointed Director of the Board of Stores and continued in his Hanlin post.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，拜中書舍人，歷戶部侍郎、端明殿學士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, Xu was made Drafting Officer of the Secretariat, then served successively as Vice Minister of Revenue and Academician of the Hall of Lucid Government.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, Xu was made Drafting Officer of the Secretariat, then served successively as Vice Minister of Revenue and Academician of the Hall of Lucid Government.

sentences.zh: 明宗重其風儀，愛其溫厚，長興中，拜中書侍郎兼刑部尚書、平章事。

translations.literal: Mingzong valued his bearing and loved his gentle warmth. In the Changxing era he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Minister of Justice, and Junior Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong valued his bearing and loved his gentle warmth. In the Changxing era he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Minister of Justice, and Junior Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 時昫入謝，遇大祠，明宗不禦中興殿，閣門白：「舊禮，宰相謝恩，須正殿通喚，請候來日。

translations.literal: When Xu came to offer thanks for his appointment, a great sacrifice was underway and Mingzong was not holding court in the Hall of Central Revival. The Gatekeepers reported: "By old custom a newly appointed chancellor must be summoned to the main hall to offer thanks. Please wait until tomorrow.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu came to offer thanks for his appointment, a great sacrifice was underway and Mingzong was not holding court in the Hall of Central Revival. The Gatekeepers reported, "By old custom a newly appointed chancellor must be summoned to the main hall to offer thanks. Please wait until tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 」樞密使趙延壽曰：「命相之制，下已數日，中謝無宜後時。

translations.literal: " Military Affairs Commissioner Zhao Yanshou said: "The edict appointing the chancellor was issued several days ago. There is no reason to delay the thanksgiving audience.
translations.idiomatic: " Military Affairs Commissioner Zhao Yanshou said, "The edict appointing the chancellor was issued several days ago. There is no reason to delay the thanksgiving audience.

sentences.zh: 」因即奏之，遂謝於端明殿。

translations.literal: " He thereupon memorialized this, and Xu offered thanks in the Hall of Lucid Government.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon memorialized this, and Xu offered thanks in the Hall of Lucid Government.

sentences.zh: 昫自端明殿學士拜相，而謝於本殿，士子榮之。

translations.literal: Xu had been promoted from Academician of the Hall of Lucid Government to chancellor and offered thanks in that very hall. Scholars took this as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Xu had been promoted from Academician of the Hall of Lucid Government to chancellor and offered thanks in that very hall. Scholars regarded this as an honor.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，兼判三司，加吏部尚書、門下侍郎，監修國史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he was additionally given charge of the Three Offices, made Minister of Personnel and Vice Director of the Chancellery, and Supervisor of the Compilation of National History.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qingtai he was additionally given charge of the Three Offices, made Minister of Personnel and Vice Director of the Chancellery, and Supervisor of the Compilation of National History.

sentences.zh: 時與同列李愚不協，動至忿爭，時論非之。

translations.literal: At the time he was at odds with his fellow councilor Li Yu and frequently quarreled in anger. Contemporary opinion disapproved of this.
translations.idiomatic: At the time he was at odds with his fellow councilor Li Yu and frequently quarreled in anger. Contemporary opinion disapproved.

sentences.zh: 未幾，俱罷知政事，昫守右僕射，以張延朗代判三司。

translations.literal: Before long both were removed from governing affairs. Xu remained as Right Vice Director and Zhang Yanlang replaced him in charge of the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Before long both were removed from governing affairs. Xu remained as Right Vice Director, and Zhang Yanlang replaced him in charge of the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 初，唐末帝自鳳翔至，切於軍用，時王玫判三司，詔問錢谷，玫具奏其數，及命賞軍，甚愆於素。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Last Emperor of Tang came from Fengxiang, military funds were urgently needed. Wang Mei was then in charge of the Three Offices. When the emperor inquired about funds and grain, Mei fully reported the numbers, but when orders came to reward the troops the amount fell far short of what had been reported.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Last Emperor of Tang came from Fengxiang, military funds were urgently needed. Wang Mei was then in charge of the Three Offices. When the emperor inquired about funds and grain, Mei fully reported the numbers, but when orders came to reward the troops the amount fell far short of what had been reported.

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：帝問王玫以府庫之實，對有數百萬在。

translations.literal: (The Zizhi Tongjian says: The emperor asked Wang Mei about the actual state of the treasury. Mei replied that several million were on hand.
translations.idiomatic: (The Zizhi Tongjian says: The emperor asked Wang Mei about the actual state of the treasury. Mei replied that several million were on hand.

sentences.zh: 既而閱實，金帛不過三萬兩匹。）〉

translations.literal: When the accounts were then verified, gold and silk amounted to no more than thirty thousand taels and bolts.)〉
translations.idiomatic: When the accounts were then verified, gold and silk amounted to no more than thirty thousand taels and bolts.)]

sentences.zh: 末帝怒，用昫代玫。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor was furious and replaced Mei with Xu.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor was furious and replaced Mei with Xu.

sentences.zh: 昫乃搜索簿書，命判官高延賞計窮詰勾，及積年殘租，或場務販負，皆虛系賬籍，條奏其事，請可征者急督之，無以償官者蠲除之。

translations.literal: Xu then searched through the ledgers and had his adjutant Gao Yanbao exhaustively audit and investigate. Arrears accumulated over years and false entries for market-bureau debts—all phantom accounts on the books—he listed in a memorial and requested that what could be collected be urgently pursued and what could not repay the state be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Xu then searched through the ledgers and had his adjutant Gao Yanbao exhaustively audit and investigate. Arrears accumulated over years and false entries for market-bureau debts—all phantom accounts on the books—he listed in a memorial and requested that what could be collected be urgently pursued and what could not repay the state be remitted.

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：清泰元年八月，免諸道逋租三百三十八萬。）〉

translations.literal: (The Zizhi Tongjian: In the eighth month of the first year of Qingtai, arrears in rent of 3.38 million were remitted across all circuits.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The Zizhi Tongjian: In the eighth month of the first year of Qingtai, arrears in rent of 3.38 million were remitted across all circuits.)]

sentences.zh: 吏民相與歌詠，唯主典怨沮。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners sang his praises together; only the responsible clerks were resentful and dejected.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners sang his praises together; only the responsible clerks were resentful and dejected.

sentences.zh: 及罷相之日，群吏相賀，昫歸，無一人從之者，蓋憎其太察故也。

translations.literal: On the day he left the chancellorship the clerks congratulated one another. When Xu returned home not a single person followed him—for they hated his excessive scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he left the chancellorship the clerks congratulated one another. When Xu returned home not a single person followed him—for they hated his excessive scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 天福初，張從賓作亂於洛陽，害皇子重乂。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu, Zhang Congbin rebelled at Luoyang and killed the imperial prince Chongyi.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianfu, Zhang Congbin rebelled at Luoyang and killed the imperial prince Chongyi.

sentences.zh: 詔為東都留守，判河南府事，尋以本官判鹽鐵。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Xu Eastern Capital Regent with charge over Henan prefecture affairs. Soon after, retaining his rank, he was given charge of the Salt and Iron Monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Xu Eastern Capital Regent with charge over Henan prefecture affairs. Soon after, retaining his rank, he was given charge of the Salt and Iron Monopoly.

sentences.zh: 未幾，奉使入契丹，還遷太子太保兼左僕射，封譙國公，俄改太子太傅。

translations.literal: Before long he was sent as envoy to the Khitan. On return he was promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Left Vice Director, enfeoffed as Duke of Qiao, and soon after made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was sent as envoy to the Khitan. On return he was promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Left Vice Director, enfeoffed as Duke of Qiao, and soon after made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 開運初，授司空、平章事，監修國史，復判三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyun he was appointed Minister of Works, Junior Grand Councilor, Supervisor of the Compilation of National History, and again given charge of the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaiyun he was appointed Minister of Works, Junior Grand Councilor, Supervisor of the Compilation of National History, and again given charge of the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 契丹主至，不改其職。

translations.literal: When the Khitan ruler arrived, his posts were not changed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan ruler arrived, his posts were not changed.

sentences.zh: 昫以眼疾乞休致，契丹主降偽命授昫守太保。

translations.literal: Xu requested retirement on account of eye disease. The Khitan ruler issued a spurious appointment making Xu Acting Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Xu requested retirement on account of eye disease. The Khitan ruler issued a spurious appointment making Xu Acting Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 契丹主北去，留於東京。

translations.literal: When the Khitan ruler departed north, Xu remained at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan ruler departed north, Xu remained at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 其年夏，以病卒，年六十。

translations.literal: That summer he died of illness. He was sixty years old.
translations.idiomatic: That summer he died of illness, aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖登極，贈太保。

translations.literal: When Han Gaozu ascended the throne, Xu was posthumously appointed Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Gaozu ascended the throne, Xu was posthumously appointed Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 初，昫避難河朔，匿於北山蘭若，有賈少瑜者為僧，輟衾袍以溫燠之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xu was fleeing turmoil in Heshuo, he hid in a mountain temple in the northern hills. A man named Jia Shaoyu was a monk there and gave up his quilted robe to warm him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Xu was fleeing turmoil in Heshuo, he hid in a mountain temple in the northern hills. A monk named Jia Shaoyu gave up his quilted robe to warm him.

sentences.zh: 及昫官達，致少瑜進士及第，拜監察御史，聞者義之。

translations.literal: When Xu reached high office he had Shaoyu pass the jinshi examination and appointed him Investigating Censor. Those who heard of this praised his sense of duty.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu reached high office he had Shaoyu pass the jinshi examination and appointed him Investigating Censor. Those who heard of this praised his sense of duty.

sentences.zh: 馮玉。

translations.literal: Feng Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yu.

sentences.zh: （案：以下有闕文。

translations.idiomatic: (Note: There is missing text below.

sentences.zh: 《歐陽史》云：字景臣，定州人。）〉

translations.literal: The Ouyang Shi says: His style was Jingchen and he was a native of Dingzhou.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The Ouyang Shi says: His style was Jingchen and he was a native of Dingzhou.)]

sentences.zh: 少帝嗣位，納馮後於中宮，後即玉之妹也。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded, he installed Lady Feng in the inner palace. The empress was Feng Yu's younger sister.
translations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor succeeded, he installed Lady Feng in the inner palace. The empress was Feng Yu's younger sister.

sentences.zh: 玉既聯戚裏，恩寵彌厚，俄自知制誥、中書舍人出為潁州團練使，遷端明殿學士、戶部侍郎，尋加右僕射，軍國大政，一以委之。

translations.literal: As Yu was now connected by imperial marriage, favor and honor grew ever thicker. Soon after serving as drafter of edicts and drafting officer of the Secretariat, he went out as military training commissioner of Yingzhou, was transferred to Academician of the Hall of Lucid Government and Vice Minister of Revenue, and soon after made Right Vice Director. All great affairs of state and army were entrusted to him alone.
translations.idiomatic: As Yu was now connected by imperial marriage, favor and honor grew ever greater. Soon after serving as drafter of edicts and drafting officer of the Secretariat, he went out as military training commissioner of Yingzhou, was transferred to Academician of the Hall of Lucid Government and Vice Minister of Revenue, and soon after made Right Vice Director. All great affairs of state and army were entrusted to him alone.

sentences.zh: （案：以下有闕文。

translations.idiomatic: (Note: There is missing text below.

sentences.zh: 《通鑒》云：玉每善承迎帝意，由是益有寵。

translations.literal: The Zizhi Tongjian says: Yu was skilled at gratifying the emperor's wishes and thereby gained ever greater favor.
translations.idiomatic: The Zizhi Tongjian says: Yu was skilled at gratifying the emperor's wishes and thereby gained ever greater favor.

sentences.zh: 嘗有疾在家，帝謂諸宰相曰：「自刺史以上，俟馮玉出，乃得除。

translations.literal: Once when he was ill at home, the emperor said to the councilors: "From prefect and above, no appointment may be made until Feng Yu has recovered and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he was ill at home, the emperor said to the councilors, "From prefect and above, no appointment may be made until Feng Yu has recovered and returned.

sentences.zh: 」其倚任如此。

translations.literal: " Such was the reliance placed on him.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the reliance placed on him.

sentences.zh: 玉乘勢弄權，四方賂遺，輻輳其門，由是朝政日壞。）〉

translations.literal: Yu abused his power; bribes from all quarters converged on his gate, and from this court governance daily worsened.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Yu abused his power; bribes from all quarters converged on his gate, and from this court governance daily worsened.)]

sentences.zh: 張彥澤陷京城，軍士爭湊其第，家財巨萬，一夕罄空。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yanze took the capital, soldiers crowded to raid his mansion. His household wealth, numbering in the tens of thousands, was emptied in a single night.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yanze took the capital, soldiers crowded to raid his mansion. His household wealth, numbering in the tens of thousands, was emptied in a single night.

sentences.zh: 翌日，玉假蓋而出，猶繞指以諂彥澤，且請令引送玉璽於契丹主，將利其復用。

translations.literal: The next day Yu went out under a parasol and still braided his fingers in fawning toward Yanze, and even asked to be allowed to convey the imperial seal to the Khitan ruler, hoping to win reinstatement.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yu went out under a parasol and still braided his fingers in fawning toward Yanze, and even asked to be allowed to convey the imperial seal to the Khitan ruler, hoping to win reinstatement.

sentences.zh: 玉從少帝北遷，契丹命為太子少保。

translations.literal: Yu followed the Young Emperor north. The Khitan appointed him Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Yu followed the Young Emperor north. The Khitan appointed him Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 至周太祖廣順二年，其子傑自幽州不告父而亡歸，玉懼譴責，尋以憂恚卒於蕃中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangshun under Zhou Taizu, his son Jie fled from Youzhou back south without telling his father. Yu feared punishment and soon died of grief and indignation among the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangshun under Zhou Taizu, his son Jie fled from Youzhou back south without telling his father. Yu feared punishment and soon died of grief and indignation among the barbarians.

sentences.zh: （《五代史補》：馮玉嘗為樞密使，有朝使馬承翰素有口辯，一旦持刺來謁玉，玉覽刺輒戲曰：「馬既有汗，宜卸下鞍。

translations.literal: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: Feng Yu once served as Military Affairs Commissioner. The court envoy Ma Chenghan was always quick with words. One day he came calling with his card. Yu read the card and joked: "If the horse already sweats, the saddle should come off.
translations.idiomatic: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: Feng Yu once served as Military Affairs Commissioner. The court envoy Ma Chenghan was always quick with words. One day he came calling with his card. Yu read the card and joked, "If the horse already sweats, the saddle should come off.

sentences.zh: 」承翰應聲曰：「明公姓馮，可謂死囚逢獄。

translations.literal: " Chenghan answered on the spot: "Your Excellency's surname is Feng—you might say a condemned man meets the prison.
translations.idiomatic: " Chenghan answered on the spot, "Your Excellency's surname is Feng—you might say a condemned man meets the prison.

sentences.zh: 」玉自以失言，遽延而謝之。）〉

translations.literal: " Yu knew he had misspoken and hurried to invite him in and apologize.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " Yu knew he had misspoken and hurried to invite him in and apologize.)]

sentences.zh: 殷鵬，字大舉，大名人也。

translations.literal: Yin Peng, styled Daju, was a native of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Peng, whose style was Daju, came from Daming.

sentences.zh: 以雋秀為鄉曲所稱，弱冠擢進士第。

translations.literal: Praised in his home district for brilliance and refinement, he passed the jinshi examination in early manhood.
translations.idiomatic: Praised in his home district for brilliance and refinement, he passed the jinshi examination in early manhood.

sentences.zh: 唐閔帝之鎮魏州，聞其名，辟為從事。

translations.literal: When the Tang Emperor Min was posted to Weizhou he heard of Peng's name and recruited him as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang Emperor Min was posted to Weizhou he heard of Peng's name and recruited him as staff officer.

sentences.zh: 及即位，命為右拾遺，歷左補闕、考功員外郎，充史館修撰，遷刑部郎中。

translations.literal: When Min ascended the throne he appointed Peng Right Reminder, then served successively as Left Supplementation Censor, Vice Director of the Board of Merit, compiler in the History Office, and Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Min ascended the throne he appointed Peng Right Reminder, then served successively as Left Supplementation Censor, Vice Director of the Board of Merit, compiler in the History Office, and Director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 鵬姿顏若婦人，而性巧媚。

translations.literal: Peng's appearance was like a woman's, and his nature clever and ingratiating.
translations.idiomatic: Peng's appearance was like a woman's, and his nature clever and ingratiating.

sentences.zh: 天福中，擢拜中書舍人，與馮玉同職。

translations.literal: During Tianfu he was promoted to Drafting Officer of the Secretariat and served alongside Feng Yu.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianfu he was promoted to Drafting Officer of the Secretariat and served alongside Feng Yu.

sentences.zh: 玉本非代言之才，所得詞目，多托鵬為之。

translations.literal: Yu had never possessed real talent for drafting edicts; most of the compositions entrusted to him were actually written by Peng on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had never possessed real talent for drafting edicts; most of the compositions entrusted to him were actually written by Peng on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 玉嘗以「姑息」字問於人，人則以「辜負」字教之，玉乃然之，當時以為笑端。

translations.literal: Yu once asked someone about the word "indulgence" (guxi); the person taught him the word "to fail in duty" (gufu). Yu accepted this, and at the time it was taken as a source of laughter.
translations.idiomatic: Yu once asked someone the meaning of the word "indulgence"; the man told him it meant "to fail in one's duty." Yu agreed, and people at court laughed at the story for years.

sentences.zh: 鵬之才比玉雖優、其纖佞過之。

translations.literal: Peng's talent, compared with Yu's, was superior, but his petty flattery exceeded Yu's.
translations.idiomatic: Peng was the better writer, but his petty flattery outdid even Yu's.

sentences.zh: 後玉出郡，借第以處之，分祿食之。

translations.literal: Later, when Yu went out to a prefecture, he lent Peng his residence to live in and shared his salary to support him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu later left for a provincial post, he lent Peng his house in the capital and shared his salary to keep him.

sentences.zh: 及玉為樞密使，擢為本院學士，每有庶僚秉鞹謁玉，故事，宰臣以履見之，鵬多在玉所，見客亦然。

translations.literal: When Yu became Commissioner of Military Affairs, Peng was promoted to academician of that bureau. Whenever subordinate officials came bearing shoes to call on Yu, by precedent the chief minister received them in slippers; Peng was often at Yu's side and received guests the same way.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu became commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, he made Peng an academician of the bureau. Junior officials would come bearing shoes to pay calls on Yu; by custom the chief minister received them in slippers. Peng was usually at Yu's side and received visitors the same way.

sentences.zh: 有丞郎王易簡退而有言，鵬銜之。

translations.literal: A director Wang Yijian spoke critically after retiring, and Peng harbored resentment against him.
translations.idiomatic: A director named Wang Yijian criticized him after leaving office, and Peng nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 及契丹入汴，有人獲玉與鵬有簽記字，皆朝廷上列有不得志欲左授者，則易簡是其首焉。

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered Bian, someone seized documents in Yu's and Peng's handwriting listing court officials who were discontented and wished to be transferred elsewhere; Yijian was named first.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan entered Bian, someone found notes in Yu's and Peng's hands listing disgruntled court officials who wanted provincial posts—and Wang Yijian headed the list.

sentences.zh: 玉既北行，鵬亦尋以病卒。

translations.literal: After Yu went north, Peng also soon died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After Yu went north with the court, Peng too soon died of illness.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：維翰之輔晉室也，罄弼諧之志，參締構之功，觀其效忠，亦可謂社稷臣矣。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: In assisting the house of Jin, Weihan exhausted his will to harmonize and aid, shared in the founding achievement, and in observing his loyal service he may be called a minister of the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: In serving the house of Jin, Weihan gave his full counsel to harmonize the realm and shared in its founding. Judged by his loyal service, he may truly be called a pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 況和戎之策，固非誤計，及國之亡也，彼以滅口為謀，此掇歿身之禍，則畫策之難也，豈期如是哉！

translations.literal: Moreover, the policy of reconciling with the barbarians was certainly no mistaken plan; yet when the state perished, they plotted to silence him and he reaped the calamity of losing his life—such is the difficulty of laying plans. Who could have expected it would come to this!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, his policy of peace with the Khitan was no mistake in itself. Yet when the state fell, others plotted to silence him and he paid with his life—the difficulty of political counsel. Who could have foreseen an end like this!

sentences.zh: 是以韓非慨慷而著《說難》者，當為此也，悲夫！

translations.literal: Thus when Han Fei wrote "The Difficulties of Persuasion" in passionate indignation, it must have been for cases like this. How lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: No wonder Han Fei wrote "The Difficulties of Persuasion" in passionate anger—for cases like this. How lamentable!

sentences.zh: 趙瑩際會風雲，優遊藩輔，雖易簀於絕域，終歸柩於故園，蓋仁信之行通於遐邇故也。

translations.literal: Zhao Ying met with the winds of fortune and moved at ease among frontier supporters. Though he changed his mat in a distant land, in the end his coffin returned to his old home—surely because conduct of benevolence and trustworthiness reaches far and near.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ying rode the tides of fortune and served comfortably as a frontier minister. Though he died in exile, his coffin at last came home to Huayin—surely because kindness and integrity are recognized even across great distances.

sentences.zh: 劉昫有真相之才，克全嘉譽；

translations.literal: Liu Xu had the talent of a true minister and was able to preserve a fine reputation;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xu had the talent of a true statesman and kept his good name to the end;

sentences.zh: 馮玉乘君子之器，終歿窮荒，其優劣可知矣。

translations.literal: Feng Yu bore the vessel of a gentleman yet died in the far wilderness—their relative worth may be known.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yu possessed a gentleman's gifts yet died in the wilderness—the contrast tells its own story.
